#2721. Celtics survive late stampede from Bucks, win 109-102

The Celtics led the Bucks by as many as 22 points on Wednesday night before the Bucks made a big comeback and briefly took the lead in the fourth. Thankfully for Boston, Paul George and Derrick White saved the day as the Celtics held on with a 109-102 win.

Jayson Tatum did not play in this game for the Celtics and Boston started Derrick White, Sam Hauser, Paul George, Hugo Gonzalez and Neemias Queta. Devin Carter was still out with mono as well. Meanwhile, the Bucks started Tyler Herro, Brayden Burries, Kyle Kuzma, Jaine Jacquez Jr. and Myles Turner and were only missing two-way player Kam Jones.

The Celtics got off to a quick start, going up 19-8 mid way through the first quarter. After Sam Hauser hit the first two shots of the game, Paul George scored 7 of the next 13 Celtics points.

The Celtics led after the first quarter 28-14. Paul George led the way with 10 points and 3 steals while playing the entire quarter. Mitchell Robinson also had 6 rebounds off of the bench.

Boston got off to a good start in the 2nd quarter as Payton Pritchard had a few baskets. It was good to see Payton Pritchard be aggressive on his first shot as well. However, a pair of Bucks threes leading to a 6-2 run lead to Joe Mazzulla calling his mandatory timeout.

The offense picked up in the 2nd quarter, as Boston led 62-41 at the half. Luka Garza led the way with 11 points and 5 rebounds while Derrick White had 9 points, 4 assists and 3 rebounds.

It was good to see the Celtics three point shooting get going, they were 10/17 in the first half after being 30% in their last 4 games, according to the NBC Sports Boston broadcast.

Boston came out flat in the 2nd half and Milwaukee took advantage. The Bucks went on a 12-5 run to open the 3rd quarter and Joe Mazzulla called a timeout. Jamie Jaquez Jr. had 5 points and Tyler Herro had 4 points during the run for Milwaukee.

The Bucks made 10 of their first 12 shots in the quarter and cut the Celtics led to 7. Back-to-back key Baylor Scheierman threes grew Boston's lead back to 13 as Milwaukee called timeout.

Payton Pritchard left the game with an right eye abrasion and he did not return to the game.

It was Tyler Herro's quarter, he had 17 points on 6/8 from the field and 2/2 from three in the 3rd quarter.

The Celtics did lead the Bucks at the end of three but what was a 21-point game at halftime was just an 8-point lead entering the fourth. Paul George's 16 points, 4 assists and 2 steals led the way for Boston.

The Bucks opened the fourth quarter on a 10-4 run and forced Joe Mazzulla to call another timeout.

Milwaukee took their first lead with 6:50 to go in the game but Boston fought back and took a 3 point lead as Taylor Jenkins called timeout.

The Celtics struggled score as they missed Tatum and Pritchard a lot. It felt like Paul George was their only source of offense late in the game.

George then stepped up to the line with under 4 minutes left and missed both free throws in a tie game.

The Celtics were able to go on a 7-0 run thank to 5 points from Derrick White to take a 104-97 lead, which Tyler Herro cut to 104-99 with two made free throws.

Paul George hit a clutch 3 to put the Celtics up 8, Ryan Rollins hit a 3 and the Bucks had a few looks to cut the Celtics lead to 2 with just over 30 seconds to go but they missed both.

Two Derrick White free throws iced it and the Celtics hung on, 109-102. George's 25 points and White's 24 points led the way for the Celtics.

Boston shot 41% from the field and 41% from three while Milwaukee shot 41% from the field and 40% from three. The Celtics next game is an NBA Cup game in Charlotte at 7 pm EST on Friday night.

#2720. Miami Dolphins Fans: Your Game 8 Takeaways

Following Sunday's loss by our Miami Dolphins to the New England Patriots, I asked the following question:

What are your overall takeaways from this afternoon's fourth game of the season between our Miami Dolphins and the New England Patriots? What are the positive and negative takeaways from this afternoon's game, as they apply to the team overall and to individual units and/or players?

Below are some of your answers and thoughts on the game-

Willis was up & down, inconsistent. I don't understand why he didn't try to utilize his legs at all – there were a couple opportunities. I also don't understand why he's under Center so much? Without a better understanding of exactly what NE was showing defensively, it just 'seemed' as though the offense ran smoother outta the gun. The pick was unfortunate but another was an easy one that was dropped.

OL had a bad day. Brewer wasn't himself & Savi gave up some whopper whiffs. Kingston was either overmatched or completely lost on a few. Paul's been solid but is showing a 2 penalty per game penchant that's getting to be too commonplace. As a whole they failed to open much running room.

Chop & Uche played pretty well but the Interior DL was terrible. Grant is scarily just, not good at the point in the middle. I thought earlier this year that IDL was going to be a strength? Not so much….

Ollie's Ollie and all that….love the fire – HATE THE FIRE!!! He's got a big mouth. He's immature. And HE'S COSTLY in an emotional way. He dances a fine line, but he's a bit overreactive and kind of a punk, always needing to yap & be heard. He should sit to start the game vs Lions….except for the fact that Jaylen Wright STINKS! But, it IS a teaching -and-learning opportunity. The kid needs to grow up.

That whiff non-sack from Chris Johnson was SO egregiously bad that it looked as if the fix was in or something? At least NE shanked the FG after, but that was really strange 'looking' – how he alligator armed a sure sack? The Safeties had another sporadic/up&down day. The down's hurt more than the up's provided.

I thought time mgt. on our last TD drive was absolutely TERRIBLE. We were going to need 2 scores….quite possibly 2 TD scores! With a little over 10 minutes we're huddling and walking back after plays, taking WAY too much time. I'm not saying go no huddle, but there should have been with much better rhythm/pace to save time AND keep NE on their heels a bit.

We got beat by a better team. Had our chances but made costly mistakes at the most inopportune times. I don't even understand how that non-1st down call for NE was overturned? I went to get a drink and came back & NE had the ball again? No angle I saw was conclusive to overturn? Guess I missed whatever they saw on review? Whatever – they fought/played hard. Made some mistakes that really cost em'. They were in the game the whole way – the 2 pt. conversion was a poorly designed play (they got some work to do there).

Just got home and cleaned up. Soggy drive, tailgate and game.

This team is coming together…they play with effort. I'm proud of what they are putting together

I wish dolphins fans put in the same effort. Bunch of sellout fans give the opponents a homefield advantage. I hate it.

We had a shot. They were in it till the end. On to Detroit.

Dolphster says the negatives and positives are obvious.

Kind of stating the obvious here, but the positive takeaway is that the team plays hard, doesn't give up, and is showing toughness and improvement even if the record doesn't reflect it. The negative takeaway is what everyone also already knows. The team is young, inexperienced, and will be digging out of the hole the previous regime put them in for a while.

dedstrk is happy with the team's week-over-week improvement.

My takeaway is they played better than I thought they would. They have gotten better every week imo. That says a lot to me.

phinette is happy they are not a Colts fan right now.

As everyone has said, the team competes well and is improving on both sides of the ball. We just lack depth and elite playmakers. I sure feel better about our team than the Colts' fans probably feel about their team right now. As always 🐬⬆️

Wildfin22 sees some bias in the refereeing.

So Washington receiver was short but Patriots receiver made the LTG 🤣🤣

dolfan8181 is another who has some issues with the refs.

get another stop on 4th down .. see raiders game for the refs to pull the okie doke.. im so sick of watching games being stolen its unreal

Wildfin22 has lost the ability to believe any longer. Fair!

Just can't understand how we played so well in the first half. Then just downright stink up the field in the 3rd quarter.But I'm realizing that we just aren't talented enough to beat any good teams.No matter how much they play hard or execute on offense. Sooner or later the lack of true talent will show up. Malik Willis just isn't good enough but he's also not experienced enough. This team may turn this around but this franchise has lost for so many seasons that I truly don't believe in them turning things around. We are on the Cleveland Browns level losing season after season. But like I'll always say until I die FINSUP!!🐬🐬

Dolphins84te says bring on the high draft picks.

Second-half adjustments (or lack therof) are killing us again this season.

I suspect that there's never going to be a consensus, especially during a painful season like this one. I'm personally trying to take it in stride and watch how all the rookies are progressing. As always, thank you all for participating in our Phinsider Question Of The Day.

#2719. Soccer-Referee hands out record 53 red cards after mass brawl erupts in Brazilian under-20s match

Nov 5 (Reuters) - An under-20s match in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais descended into complete chaos, with the referee having to hand out a record ‌53 red cards following a massive brawl.

The brawl took place during the first ‌leg of a state championship semifinal match between Uberlandia and Mamore on Sunday.

In his report of the match, referee ​Fernando Patrick Drosghic Modesto said the trouble began early in the second half, when a number of Uberlandia officials invaded the field of play after one of their players was sent off.

The match was halted for 40 minutes and eventually restarted, with Mamore going on to score in ‌the ninth minute of stoppage time ⁠to take a 3-1 lead.

According to reports in Brazilian media, Mamore player Davi taunted Uberlandia players during the goal celebrations, which sparked a massive ⁠brawl and led to a deluge of red cards.

A total of 43 players and 8 members of the coaching staff were sent off, while 2 Uberlandia board members were also dismissed, taking ​the tally ​up to 53.

"In the 54th minute of the ​second half, a generalized brawl broke ‌out, making it impossible to show the red cards and to carry out the match-closing protocol," Drosghic Modesto wrote in his report.

"Therefore, owing to all the turmoil and the lack of security, I declared the match ended."

Drosghic Modesto added that a police report had been filed over threats made against the referee and that Mamore's team had vandalised the dressing room after ‌the match.

The previous Guinness World Record for the most ​red cards shown in a match was 36, which ​occurred in February 2011 during a ​fifth-division match in Argentina between Atletico Claypole and Victoriano Arenas.

On Wednesday, Uberlandia ‌said it would be forfeiting the second ​leg of the semifinal ​in a "gesture of fair play," since Mamore did not have enough eligible players to field a team.

The forfeit saw Mamore qualify for the final of the tournament.

"The club ​has also not remained silent: ‌the appropriate disciplinary measures regarding those involved have already been taken internally, because ​athletic development is, above all, a matter of personal development," Uberlandia added.

(Reporting by ​Aadi Nair in Bengaluru; Editing by Thomas Derpinghaus)

#2718. NFL Week 9 Injury Report: Jeremiyah Love hits IR, Lamar Jackson likely done for season, and more

Staying up to date on NFL injury news is of the utmost importance for fantasy football success. The article below tracks all fantasy-relevant players currently listed on their team's injury report and provides fantasy managers with actionable recommendations as new information rolls in.

Check back for updates from Tuesday through Saturday.

**UPDATED AS OF WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 4 AT 8:00 PM ET**

The Bills emerged from their Week 8 win over the Ravens absent any fantasy-relevant injuries.

Impact: Willis practiced in full with the same injury last week before rushing just once on game day. The injury could be limiting him in-game, though he remains a QB2 against the Lions.

Impact: Kayton Allen (quad) was limited. He could end up challenging Wright for the No. 2 role at some point.

Achane suffered a torn ACL in the team's Week 3 loss to the Chiefs, ending his season.

Impact: Achane's unfortunate season-ending injury creates opportunity for Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright. The timing of the injury makes it likely that Achane is able to fully recover before the start of the 2027 regular season.

Hollins departed the team's Week 4 win over the Bills with a calf injury and did not return. He was placed on injured reserve in Week 5. Hollins resumed practicing in Week 9.

Impact: Hollins' potential return clouds the pass-catching corps' Week 9 prospects.

Doubs was placed on injured reserve following a shoulder injury sustained in Week 6. He will miss the next four games, at minimum.

Impact: The Patriots have now played only 33 offensive snaps with both Doubs and A.J. Brown on the field together this season after Doubs was injured on his second offensive snap in Week 6. Brown returned from injured reserve in Week 6 and should have the runway to return WR1 numbers while Doubs remains sidelined.

Brown was limited on Wednesday but downgraded to "DNP" Thursday and Friday, ultimately ruled out for Week 8 against the Dolphins. Brown remains sidelined to begin Week 9.

Impact: DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism stepped up in Brown's absence, but Mack Hollins (calf) could return this week, adding volatility for fantasy purposes.

Henderson was ruled out Saturday with an illness after missing practice Wednesday and Thursday. He remains sidelined to begin Week 9.

Impact: Rhamondre Stevenson should operate as a clear workhorse for as long as Henderson remains sidelined, while Corey Kiner is in line to serve as the primary change-of-pace option.

Henry left early in Week 8 after injuring his foot. He did not practice the following Wednesday.

Impact: Eli Raridon vaults into the streaming TE1 tier.

Hall has missed the previous five games but is tentatively expected to return in Week 9 against the Chiefs. However, he remains limited to begin Week 9.

Impact: Taylor should face the Chiefs this weekend, though he is only a TE2/3.

Jackson returned from an ankle injury in Week 8 and made it all of one offensive snap before suffering a thumb injury that is likely to sideline him for the remainder of the regular season.

Impact: Jackson's absence is the biggest hit to the fantasy value of alpha receiver Zay Flowers, who falls to a mid-range WR2 in rest of season rankings.

Huntley suffered a season-ending turf toe injury in the team's Week 8 loss to the Bills. Rookie Joe Fagnano came on in relief against the Bills and could not sustain drives, leaving the team in dire need of consistent quarterback play. Fagnano is reportedly dealing with an ankle injury and was seen wearing an ankle guard/brace in practice Tuesday. Fagnano will start on Thursday night, though the Ravens are expected to start trade acquisition Jacoby Brissett in Week 10. The Jaguars D/ST is an elite play in Week 9.

#2717. Jalen Brunson's 22 first-quarter points kickstart Knicks' 135-105 smackdown of Bulls

The Knicks took advantage of a floundering Chicago Bulls defense -- ranked 29th of 30 in the league -- Wednesday night, winning their third-straight game and their fourth in the last five with a final score of 135-105.

-- New York came out of the gate fast, stunning a young Bulls team into a state of near paralysis. Chicago surrendered 10 points off of turnovers through the first 13 minutes of play, while the Knicks, who have struggled in transition so far this season, let up none across the same span. The Bulls also faltered from beyond the arc, missing 20-straight threes in the middle stretch of the first half. Led by Jalen Brunson's 26 first-half points, New York went into the break with a dominating 32-point lead (84-53).

-- After struggling to find the basket through the first few games of the season -- and missing his first three of Wednesday's game -- Brunson looked back to peak form in the first quarter, scoring a staggering 22 points in 11 first-quarter minutes. Collectively, the Bulls only scored 21 in the opening frame.

Even with significantly decreased minutes in the back half of the contest, Brunson continued to produce, finishing the night with 33 points, two rebounds, and four assists.

-- The Knicks went 24-for-26 from the charity stripe in the first half. OG Anunoby contributed nearly half of those points.

He drew 10 free throws in the first 14 minutes of play -- marking the second-straight game in which he earned eight attempts -- and landed every one for 10 of his 18 first-half points. A third personal foul with 8:48 left in the opening half stifled his run as he sat for the next five minutes, and while he drew two more foul shots before the half wound down, he only hit one. Still, his 11 made free throws tied a career-best mark for most in the first half.

-- Karl-Anthony Towns finished the game with his eighth-consecutive double-double (17 points, 12 rebounds), completing the set less than halfway through the third despite only recording one shot from the field by the end of the first half. He opened the third quarter with two back-to-back threes and only turned up the heat from there.

Toward the end of the second frame, Towns jumped up to shoot a three but was met by Chicago forward Zach Collins, who knocked the ball out of Towns' hand. On his way down, Collins stepped on Towns' toe and knocked him over, triggering a review for a flagrant foul. However, because Collins' foot landed on top of Towns' rather than below, the move was ruled as a common foul instead, and Towns earned three free throws. He made all three.

-- With Josh Hart sidelined due to ankle soreness, Landry Shamet joined New York's starting five for the first time this season. The shooting guard more than earned the right Monday, lifting the Knicks to a win against the Brooklyn Nets with a game-leading 22 points.

Right off the bat, Shamet landed two buckets, scoring the Knicks' first four points. His production slowed down after that, but he finished with seven points, two rebounds, two assists, and a plus-21 rating.

-- For the second game in a row -- and third in the last week -- New York's bench combined for 40-plus points (53 on Wednesday). This time, Jordan Clarkson and Dalton Knecht led the way.

In his first game as a Knick, Knecht scored 10 points in 13 minutes played. His first points came from a tip-in dunk on a Shamet miss. His second -- a 25-foot step-back jump shot -- put the Knicks at 84 first-half points, tying the franchise record for most points scored in the opening 24 minutes of a game. He also added seven rebounds and an assist.

Clarkson, who also scored 10, went 4-for-9 from the field and 2-for-2 from three.

Mohammed Diawara, who first subbed in for Anunoby with five minutes left in the first, collected three points, one rebound, and one block in three first-quarter minutes. He finished with eight points, tied with James Wiseman for second-most on the bench.

Late in the third, Miles McBride leapt up for a 24-foot jumper from deep at the play clock buzzer before he was knocked over, drawing a foul and turning the sequence into a four-point play. He finished with seven points.

-- All 14 available Knicks made an appearance. Everyone except Jose Alvarado and Pacome Dadiet played 11 minutes or more. They each played nine.

The star point guard finished 10-for-17 from the field, 5-for-10 from three-point range, and 8-for-9 from the free throw line en route to a season-best 33-point performance. No other Knick surpassed 18 points.

After a few days of rest, New York will be back in action Saturday night when they take on the Cleveland Cavaliers. Tip off is scheduled for 8 p.m.

#2716. Michael Carrick insists he will NOT be sacked as Man United manager - despite side slipping closer to relegation zone after Chelsea defeat

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER

Published: 12:33 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 12:50 EDT, 31 October 2026

Michael Carrick believes he will cling onto his job as Manchester United head coach despite watching helplessly as his team slid closer towards the relegation zone at Chelsea.

Goals from Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer – who converted a penalty after Lisandro Martinez was sent off for picking up two yellow cards in the space of 82 seconds – consigned United to a 2-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge as they sank to 17th(check) place in the Premier League.

Earlier this week, Carrick was given more time by Old Trafford bosses to turn the club’s disastrous season around, but he is now without a win in nine games.

Asked if he will be in charge for Tuesday’s Champions League clash with Roma, he replied: ‘Yes. I'm just looking forward to getting the boys ready for the midweek now.’

The 20-time champions of England are faced with the humiliation of dropping into the bottom three and it was put to Carrick, a player and coach at United stretching back two decades, that seeing the club in such a position must be hurting him.

‘Yeah, pretty much exactly that,’ he said. ‘There is a lot of emotion. We're a great football club and we want to win football matches. Things have gone against us in a big way and unravelled quickly.

Man United are now without a win in nine games in all competitions, their longest such run since October-November 1988

‘There is no hiding from the fact that we haven't won enough games. There's no words that I'm going to explain to you now that makes it any different, it's not going to change it.

‘You can look at how far you can move up the league quite quickly if you win football matches. So that's the way it's got to be approached, for sure.’

Carrick insisted that he didn’t feel let down by Martinez, but did not even look at the Argentine as he left the pitch.

‘It has a major importance on the game. A huge moment. I think that is pretty obvious really,’ added Carrick. ‘The second goal and losing the man at that stage had a big influence on it, for sure.’

The United fans continued to give Carrick their support while once again turning on the club’s owners, the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and director of football Jason Wilcox.

Meanwhile, Xabi Alonso admitted Estevao’s positive performance will give him a selection headache after the wonderkid showed Chelsea what they have been missing.

Morgan Rogers' brilliant solo goal set Chelsea on their way to victory

The 19-year-old Brazilian was handed his first Premier League start of the season and scored two disallowed goals for offside as well as creating several other opportunities.

‘He’s given me reasons (to pick him),’ said Alonso. ‘This is football and sometimes you don’t get what you want, but the best way to show it is not by being angry, it’s by being competitive and Este has done it really well.’

Alonso also hailed Romeo Lavia after the 22-year-old Belgian filled in for the unwell Jordan Henderson in midfield on short notice, and was arguably this game’s best performer.

‘From a midfielder point of view, for me it has been a top, top performance,’ Alonso said. ‘He's done so many things right. He’s been always connecting the defence with the attacker players, he's been able to switch the game, he's taken many right decisions, he's been very dynamic, competitive. I'm very happy for him and he deserves a huge recognition for his performance.’

#2715. Everything to know for Bengals vs. Falcons in Madrid

The Cincinnati Bengals are in Madrid to face the Atlanta Falcons in NFL Week 9. The game is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. on Nov. 8 and the game will be broadcast locally on NBC/WLWT-TV and nationally on NFL Network.

Cincinnati (5-2) is coming off a win over the Tennessee Titans and Atlanta (3-5) is coming off a loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

The Bengals will meet with the media today as head coach Zac Taylor will host a press conference for media in Madrid and players also will be available for interviews.

Here's what you need to know for the week:

The Bengals are practicing on Nov. 5 and 6. The team will not have media availability on Nov. 7. The Bengals vs. Falcons Week 9 game is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. Eastern on Nov. 8.

The Bengals traveled to Madrid on Nov. 3 and will fly back home after the game on Nov. 8. Cincinnati will host the Pittsburgh Steelers on Nov. 15 at Paycor Stadium on "Sunday Night Football."

Madrid is located in the Central European Time zone, which is six hours ahead of the Eastern Time zone. The Week 9 game between the Bengals and Falcons will take place at 3:30 p.m. locally in Madrid, which is 9:30 a.m. Eastern.

The Bengals are 0-1-1 in two international games. Both games were played at Wembley Stadium in London.

The first time the Bengals played overseas was in 2016 against the Washington Commanders. The game ended in a 27-27 tie. The last time the Bengals were overseas was Zac Taylor's first season as head coach and Cincinnati lost 24-10 to the Los Angeles Rams. The Bengals would eventually meet the Rams in Super Bowl 56, suffering a 23-20 loss.

The Falcons have played one more game than the Bengals abroad and have a win as well. Atlanta's first game was a 21-20 loss to the Detroit Lions at Wembley Stadium in 2014, which was followed by a 27-20 win over the New York Jets at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London in 2021. The Falcons most recently had a 23-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2023.

The Bengals lead the all-time series against the Falcons at 10-5. The two teams most recently met Oct. 23, 2022 at Paycor Stadium and the Bengals won 35-17. The 2022 win made it a three-game winning streak for the Bengals against the Falcons.

#2714. Recap: Wizards plagued by familiar issues in 120-105 loss to Hawks

The Washington Wizards' 120-105 loss to the Atlanta Hawks at Capital One Arena on Wednesday followed a script similar to the team's first three defeats this season. The home team was outshot from long range and gave up far too many offensive rebounds.

Anthony Davis got off to a hot start, scoring 6 of the Wizards' first 8 points. He tweaked his ankle just over a minute into the contest after landing on AJ Dybantsa's foot on a closeout. But Davis still finished with 10 points through the first 12 minutes.

Despite Washington seemingly playing well, Atlanta stayed ahead with the three-ball. The Hawks hit 8 three-pointers in the first quarter alone to take a 37-32 lead after one.

Dybantsa had a tough night offensively. He looked out of control at times and failed to get a veteran whistle on some of his drives. He took his frustrations out on the rim with a two-handed jam in the second quarter.

A triple from old friend CJ McCollum gave the Hawks a 16-point lead with 2:13 to play. The Wizards closed the half on a 9-0 run to cut the deficit to 68-61 at the half. Davis led all scorers with 18 points, along with 6 rebounds and 2 blocks at the break.

Kyshawn George ran point whenever Young was off the floor. He evidently picked up a few things from the All-Star point guard, as he repeatedly found Davis and Deandre Ayton for easy baskets around the rim.

The defense was much improved in the third quarter, but it was the offense lagged behind. Washington finally built up some momentum late when Trae hit a step-back three that got the team within four points of Atlanta.

Will Riley missed a clean look at a three on the following possession that would have gotten the Wizards to within one. The Hawks made it hurt as another old friend, Corey Kispert, connected on a four-point play on the other end.

George had a huge fourth quarter. He came alive with 12 points in the period but did not have much support from his Wizards teammates as the Hawks pulled away for the 15-point victory.

The Hawks more than tripled (19) the Wizards (6) in three-point makes. Atlanta already had Washington's three-point total midway through the first quarter. The Wizards also gave up 19 offensive rebounds as Dyson Daniels and Onyeka Okongwu combined to grab 33 boards.

Davis powered through his ankle injury to tally 26 points and 10 rebounds. George flashed more of his star potential with 25 points on 10-of-14 shooting, on top of his 7 assists.

Dybantsa and Tre Johnson both struggled from the field in this one. The No. 1 overall pick had his first poor outing offensively, with 9 points on a 4-of-12 clip. He also badly missed on 3 of his 4 free-throw attempts. Johnson looked rattled after his first few misses. He continued to force his shots through garbage time, making just 1 of his 9 attempts.

The Wizards get an immediate chance to avenge the loss when they head to Atlanta to face the Hawks on Friday for their second NBA Cup game.

#2712. 2026 NHL free agent tracker: Patrick Kane returns to Blackhawks on two-year contract

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

NHL free agency has slowed down in late July, but some notable names are still coming off the board. Most notably, Patrick Kane is returning to the Chicago Blackhawks on a two-year contract worth $16 million, the team announced on Thursday.

Already a Chicago legend and future Hall of Famer, Kane won three Stanley Cups and a slew of individual awards with the franchise that selected him with the No. 1 overall pick in 2007. Kane's first stint with the Blackhawks lasted 16 seasons, and he piled up 446 goals and 779 assists in 1,161 games. Kane ranks inside the top five of just about every statistical category in franchise history, and he will get the chance to keep climbing those lists over the next two years.

The Blackhawks sent Kane to the New York Rangers at the 2023 NHL trade deadline, and he played just 19 regular season games there before hitting free agency the next summer. Hip surgery delayed Kane's decision until November of that year, but he ultimately landed with the Detroit Red Wings, where he's spent the last three seasons.

Last season was Kane's best with Detroit, and it proved that he still had some gas left in the tank, at least offensively. Kane posted 16 goals and 41 assists in 67 games -- with 19 of those points coming on the power play.

In his second stint with the Blackhawks, Kane will add another level of playmaking to the power play, and he should strengthen a top six forward group that's bereft of proven talent. Kane will also be an excellent mentor and sounding board for fellow No. 1 overall pick, Connor Bedard, who is set to miss the first month of the season after undergoing shoulder surgery.

Kane isn't the player he once was, but he'll give Chicago a bit more pop at the top of the lineup, and his first game back in a Blackhawks jersey will be a huge night for the city.

Here are the top 30 NHL free agents as we track where each one lands.

#2709. What happened to Kon Knueppel? Hornets star's season debut ends after 6 minutes

The Charlotte Hornets were eagerly awaiting the regular season debut of second-year star and Rookie of the Year runner-up Kon Knueppel.

The Hornets ruled Knueppel out for the remainder of their game Wednesday, Nov. 4 against the Brooklyn Nets with left leg soreness. This is particularly concerning because Knueppel had been sidelined with a left hamstring strain.

After the game, Hornets coach Charles Lee told the local broadcast that he did not have an update on Knueppel and said he would be evaluated once the team returned to Charlotte later Wednesday.

Although there didn't appear to be a specific play in which Knueppel got hurt, he exited shortly after he dribbled the ball off his foot. During the play, Knueppel tried to dribble the ball behind his back but it caromed off his right leg, forcing him to take a small step as he tried to recover it. Immediately after the play, Knueppel limped but tried to stay in the game before quickly heading to the bench. He eventually went into the locker room and did not return.

Knueppel scored 3 points, all from free throws, missed his only shot attempt, a 3-pointer, and committed 2 turnovers in 5:51 on the floor against the Nets. He did not record any other statistic.

"Hopefully I can contribute in a capacity similar to last year, and with all the offseason work that I put in, even more," Knueppel told the Hornets broadcast in a pregame interview. "It might take me a little bit to get to that full capability, but tonight I'll be ready to go and help us get a win."

Last season, his first in the NBA after the Hornets selected him with the No. 4 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, Knueppel recorded 18.5 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game. He converted 3-pointers at a 42.5% clip and lost out to his college teammate at Duke, Cooper Flagg, for the Rookie of the Year honor.

#2708. 2026-27 NHL season predictions: Expert picks for Stanley Cup playoffs, champion and major awards this season

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Following a brief offseason and an expedited preseason, the 2026-27 NHL season has arrived. Before the puck drops on opening night, we have some predictions to make.

If this season feel like it's staring earlier than usual, that's because it is. The NHL is adopting an 84-game regular season, which just means more hockey for the rest of us. That also means a long and arduous journey to the Stanley Cup is ever so slightly more difficult.

So, what will that journey look like? The Carolina Hurricanes are looking to defend their title as Cup champions, but they'll have to contend with a deep Eastern Conference and some real juggernauts in the Western Conference. With that in mind, we logged our expert predictions for the playoff field in each conference -- and there were a few surprises -- before making our Stanley Cup Final selections.

We also called our shot on the winners of each major individual award. Connor McDavid is looking for his fourth Hart Trophy, but he's got some competition from an up-and-coming superstar in his own division. Races for the Norris Trophy and Vezina Trophy should be pretty wide open, and unexpected candidates always emerge throughout the season.

It should be a fun season in the NHL, so follow along with all our coverage at CBS Sports. Let's get things kicked off with the season preview and predictions, which will of course be 100% accurate.

Baumgartner: I don't see many new faces entering the conversation when it comes to the Eastern Conference playoff race. A healthy Florida Panthers side will slot themselves right back towards the top of the Atlantic, and a revamped Washington Capitals side should be able to make some noise in the Metropolitan. Besides that, I have six 2026 playoff teams returning to the dance in 2027.

Nivison: As much as I hate to go with chalk in preseason predictions -- because it rarely happens that way -- there's no denying the top dogs in the West. The Avalanche and Stars are the class of the Central Division, and the Golden Knights should pound a pitiful Pacific Division into a pulp. Things get more interesting behind those clear Cup contenders, and I'm projecting another significant leap forward from the Mammoth. I also think Macklin Celebrini will be successful in dragging the Sharks to the playoffs in his third NHL season.

Nivison -- Columbus Blue Jackets: The Blue Jackets have been agonizingly close to the playoffs in each of the last two seasons, and I think they get over the hump in 2026-27. There are still questions in Columbus. Can Adam Fantilli be a franchise player at center? Is the forward group as a whole good enough to keep pace in a competitive Eastern Conference? Still, I am sure the Blue Jackets have a really strong blue line, led by Norris Trophy winner Zach Werenski, and goaltender Jet Greaves is on track to become a Vezina Trophy candidate. Internal improvements from the young core will then get Columbus above the cut line.

Baumgartner -- San Jose Sharks: The Sharks narrowly missed out on the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, finishing just four points short of the second wild card. San Jose added a good group of veterans over the summer, but the most important offseason move was selecting Ivar Stenberg with the No. 2 pick in the Draft. Stenberg joins the youth movement in San Jose, which is spearheaded by new captain Macklin Celebrini, who broke the Sharks single-season points record with 115 last season. The Sharks are a better team than they were last year, and with Celebrini entering his third season as a legit Hart Trophy contender, this team won't be fun to play against.

Nivison: Yes, the Mammoth have a brutal path coming out of the Central Divison, but just close your eyes and imagine this scenario with me. Logan Cooley becomes a superstar center. Dylan Guenther hits 50 goals. Dmitry Simashev asserts himself as a budding top-four defenseman. Anders Lee and Vincent Trocheck provide necessary veteran depth. Now open your eyes. Utah is your Western Conference champion.

Unfortunately for the Mammoth, they will run into a refreshed Panthers team that now has double-barreled Tkachuks. Last season, we found out that all it takes to stop Florida is to hope all of its key players miss significant time with injury. The long offseason was probably a blessing in disguise as it allowed the Panthers to get healthy, and that's bad news for everyone else. The structure in front of the crease will limit some of the volatility we saw from Jacob Markstrom in New Jersey, and Florida wins its third Stanley Cup in four years.

Baumgartner: Before last season, the Carolina Hurricanes' kryptonite was the Eastern Conference Final. The Hurricanes were able to overcome their demons and win the East before ultimately taking home the franchise's first Stanley Cup since 2006. In the West, the Dallas Stars have been running into the same problem. After three straight seasons ending in the Western Conference Final, the Stars regressed last postseason, flaming out in the first-round to the Minnesota Wild. The Central Division will once again be a gauntlet, but I'm ready for Dallas to take the next step and reach the Stanley Cup Final.

While Dallas has continued to fall short in recent years, the Panthers have done the opposite. The Panthers made three consecutive Stanley Cup Final appearances, winning back-to-back Cups in 2023-24 and 2024-25. Last season, Florida's three-peat attempt came to a halt on day one of training after captain Aleksander Barkov went down with a non-contact injury, tearing both the ACL and MCL in his right knee. An offseason of healing for Barkov, and the rest of the banged up Panthers, has the team refreshed entering September for the first time in years. With nearly the entire 2025 Stanley Cup winning core still on the team and Brady Tkachuk added to the fold, Florida looks ready to win its third Stanley Cup in four seasons.

Nivison: Celebrini should have won the Hart Trophy last season, but for some incomprehensible reason, he wasn't even a finalist. This year, Celebrini replicates that performance and gets San Jose to the postseason to take home his first MVP award at age 20. Hughes posts a career year in his first full season with the Wild, and Spencer Carberry gets his flowers for winning the Metro Division after missing the playoffs last year.

Baumgartner: McDavid's ability to take over a game was evident nearly every time he touched the ice last season. His 24 points (11 goals,13 assists) in the final 14 games of the regular season -- without Leon Draisaitl in the lineup -- was one of the many reasons I put him No. 1 on my Hart Trophy ballot. With just two years left on his current contract, desperation may start to kick in to get the job in Edmonton, which would lead to another MVP-caliber season. Barkov is healthy and the frontrunner to win his fourth Selke, and Dahlin will have another strong season to take home his first career Norris Trophy.

#2706. Team effort sees the Nets beat the Hornets, winning for the firs time at home 114-104

One of the few silver linings to the Brooklyn Nets' 1-6 start was the supposedly easier stretch of opponents awaiting them after it. As Jayson Tatum game-winners, injuries, and second half collapses have all hacked away at early season morale, that was the only thing left to hold onto.

Like a jagged ledge in a damp cave, it was a ballsy thing to reach for. After all, the Hornets had beaten Brooklyn badly at home just two weeks ago.

Well, you know what they say. Audentes fortuna iuvat.

Brooklyn began this one with a starting five featuring Nolan Traoré, Chaney Johnson, Michael Porter Jr., Julius Randle, and Day'Ron Sharpe for a fourth straight game. Their first minutes brought mixed results. Day'Ron Sharpe picked up his first foul of the contest just six seconds into it, and then his second with us less than two minutes deep. That gave us a premature introduction to Mo Wagner.

But even if you discount the foul trouble, Brooklyn's early defense looked flimsy. Either due to slow rotations or off offensive rebounds, the Nets gave up warm-up threes for Charlotte during pre-game shoot around sessions.

Luckily for Brooklyn, even in those shoot around sessions, nobody makes 'em all. Charlotte missed all of 'em, beginning the game 0-7 from downtown. The Nets, benefitting from another assertive start at the other end from Nolan Traoré and more efficient one from Julius Randle, led until the 3:47 mark of the first. The Hornets went ahead on a four point play, after Naz Reid hit a three as Wagner got caught with his elbow in Grayson Allen's chest, which warranted a flagrant foul penalty. Don't you hate when that happens?

Had Mikel Brown Jr. not come in and convert an and-one finish and then a step-back three in Moussa Diabaté's face in back-to-back possessions, the Nets might've been down double digits after the opening frame. Instead, they trailed by just three.

MBJ kept the showing going in the subsequent quarter, hitting a turnaround jumper, dropping two assists, and taking a charge at the defensive end all within the span of three minutes. One of the dimes, a no-look, behind the back dish while soaring through the air. If you can't even conceptualize what that would look like, I don't blame you…

At the break, Brown Jr. had nine points, three assists, a steal, and a block in 13 minutes. He would finish with a career-high 18 points on 6-11 shooting along with three assists. For Brooklyn, he trailed only Randle at the halfway point, who had 14 points, three boards, and an assists. Michael Porter Jr. got hot late in the second, adding nine points and 3-8 shooting.

However, the Hornets maintained a seven point lead going into the break, even with three extra turnovers and after shooting 41% from the field against a Brooklyn defense that'd begun playing with an extra layer of physicality. As the Nets did better to shoot and take care of the ball better, Charlotte manufactured a seven extra points at the free throw line.

Apparently running New York's playbook from Monday night, the Hornets also hit an abundance of corner threes down the stretch of the second. Grayson Allen, who led the Hornets with 20 points at the break, got two of his five made threes in the half from that areas.

During the break, the Nets announced that Noah Clowney would sit out the remainder of the game with right knee soreness. Chaney Johnson still started the third with the original group, but that gave us our first non-garbage time minutes of the season for Danny Wolf, who came in for Johnson less than three minutes deep in the frame.

The new lineup quickly made a case for itself as a mainstay in Jordi Fernández's rotation. Capped off by a triple from Wolf himself, that group went on an 11-0 run in three minutes, giving the Nets a lead for the first time since the 5:42 point of the second.

"Danny coming in, you know, and contributing right away like that, that takes a lot of a lot of readiness and a lot of discipline to not play for so many games and come in in the second half and to contribute the way he did," Porter Jr. said. "I mean, I always thought Danny was a special player, and I've said that since he got here. I think he can do so many things at the basketball court, and I'm really happy that he got the opportunity."

"Obviously in the NBA, there's gonna be times, especially early in your career, that you might not be in the rotation, and that was the case when we started the year," Wolf said. "Everyone emphasizes and preaches that you have to be ready, and you hear it over and over, just make sure you're doing all your work and doing all of the things to make sure that when your name gets called, you're ready. And I tried taking advantage of all the time I had, and when the first called my name in the second half, I was ready, and I was looking for that opportunity and tried to do anything I could to help the team win."

The latter half of the third period then gave us some fun back-and-forth action as neither team managed to separate by more than a bucket or two. We even got a surprise cameo from Terance Mann, who's either played early or not at all so far this year, coming in with around three and a half to go in the frame. Like the quarter before, Brown Jr. also finished it scoring with a three he carved up for himself in isolation, which things 80-80 entering the fourth.

There, Brooklyn began the scoring with triples from Randle, Wolf, and Brown Jr. to extend a six point lead.

A few moments after his triple, Brown Jr. turned it over trying to sneak an interior feed in for Sharpe, and then left his assignment trying to steal the ball back, leading to an open dunk for Charlotte and a Fernández timeout. The shot-making was there, but so were the headaches, as they often are with the league's younger teams.

To win, the Nets would need proceed with one of those things and ditch other latter. Michael Porter Jr. got them off to a solid start in the right direction.

After Fernández's timeout, MPJ got in on the action with three of his own makes from deep across Brooklyn's next five possessions. He didn't do anything fancy to get them — and didn't need to — just ducking hard around screens and rising up to fire without hesitation. That was enough anything to keep it a multi-possession lead even as Reid put in nine points in the period's first five minutes.

"I just told the guys like at the beginning of fourth quarter, like let's be a team that learns from our mistakes, tries to not make the same mistake twice," Porter Jr. said. "We were in the same position a couple nights ago in New York and fell apart in the fourth quarter. So I mean, that's what good teams do, rowing teams do, is they learn from their failure and they try to not do that same thing again. So I was proud of everybody."

The Nets went up 10 with 3:49 to go after Sharpe got up for a rejection that sprung Wolf on the break, who finished and-one through a back-pedaling Sion James. That rejection might as well have been an assist for Sharpe, but he got eight of those tonight anyway — a career high to go along with his six points and five rebounds.

"I think the biggest staple of our team, especially our offensive identity, is you're supposed to be playing fast," Wolf said. "We use the terminology 'pace and space,' and I feel like there's times when we do it great, and I think there's times with my play style that I can really help us push the ball up the floor, make simple passes, to start the break. I think you get those, and you get momentum, and momentum is what helps win a basketball game."

Without Kon Knueppel, who exited due to left leg soreness, and Brandon Miller shooting 1-12 from the field, the Hornets had no choice but to settle for Naz Reid isolation possessions. And the Nets, conscious by that point of the Charlotte's intention to hunt switches with their big man, were ahead, shading and dropping in defense in a timely fashion to limit their opponent's scoring.

Of course, Miller hit his first three of the game after a timeout a few sequences, but Traoré just kept on driving, and scoring, adding six points in the fourth. Fernández also won a big challenge to give Porter Jr. free throws that extended the lead to 12 with under two to go when we otherwise would have been Charlotte ball. He also rolled the dice closing with a lineup featuring Traoré, Mann, Porter Jr., Wolf, and Sharpe, as Randle only logged three fourth period minutes. Fernández credited the three-time All-Star for being "selfless" postgame.

"I called him in to sub in, and then they took it to 10 or 11, and Julius the one just like letting them roll," Fernández said. "So you see, every single instance of great things that have to happen in the game, and even a bit of being Julius, who is and how important it is for us, I think that that was huge."

Randle still finished with 22 points, four assists, and three rebounds while shooting 7-13 from the field. Porter Jr. led with 26 points while shooting 8-17 from the field. He also grabbed 10 boards. After Brown Jr., Traoré came next with 16 points on 7-11 shooting along with two assists and three steals. Wolf added 12 points, dished out three assists, and grabbed five boards while shooting 4-6 from the field.

That closing group also looked nothing like the uncoordinated and out of place team we saw last time out, running the clock down like a methodical NFL offense.

With all the active players logging minutes, almost all of them making an impact at one point or another, and Fernández pressing all the right buttons along the way, it was as good of a team effort as you've seen from this group in some time. It also got the Nets their first home win of the season.

Final: Brooklyn Nets 114, Charlotte Hornets 104

Day'Ron Sharpe had recorded a career-high eight assists in tonight's game vs. Charlotte.

Rookie Mikel Brown Jr. had a career-best 18 points on 3-5 3PT with four assists off the bench.

Michael Porter Jr. led Brooklyn with 26 points and 10 rebounds in tonight's win vs. Charlotte for his second double-double of the season. It was his 26th career game with 25+ PTS and 10+ REB after a career-high eight such games last season.

As mentioned, the Nets announced at halftime that Noah Clowney would be out for the remainder of the game with right knee soreness. We'll provide updates on him as they're made available.

Brooklyn begins its first legitimate road trip of the season next with a trip down south to face the Atlanta Hawks. At the time of writing, Atlanta is 4-4 with wins over the Pacers, Cavaliers, Hornets, and Magic, and losses against the Pelicans, Heat, and two to the Rockets.

The Nets have lost five straight to the Hawks. Their last win came in March 2025 in a game where Keon Johnson, Tyrese Martin, and Jalen Wilson started. This next one tips off on Saturday at 7:30 p.m. EST.

#2699. Full throttle Brighton have the depth, quality and guile to hang in there with Arsenal and Man City, writes JACK GAUGHAN, as individual mistakes haunt Enzo Maresca's men in latest defeat

Published: 13:16 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 14:38 EDT, 31 October 2026

A game condensed into 15 seconds. Jeremy Doku loses possession on the touchline but won't have that, thundering into a tackle to recollect and then sets off beating two men. He seems in the mood for destruction.

An expectant Etihad is up, the Premier League's trickiest winger cutting loose and Manchester City are in. One calm final ball and an equaliser is on.

Doku tries to find a lurking Erling Haaland, or at least it appears so, because the pass is so bad that Brighton are already storming upfield themselves.

Around 15 minutes after that, Fabian Hurzeler is roaring at his bench. He is chest bumping substitutes and backroom staff with defiant pride, vindication of the words spoken about seeking revenge in the immediately aftermath of losing on penalties here in the cup a matter of days ago.

Brighton stayed in Manchester after Wednesday night and Hurzeler spent that time plotting, organising the battle plan to topple league leaders who have been fallible defensively under Enzo Maresca this season but are producing scintillating attacking moments.

Hurzeler leaves the north west following a little getaway at the Lowry Hotel having drawn and won against City over the course of two 90 minutes. His stock is soaring, his side a fascination and the faint chorus of 'we're gonna win the league' from the away end might just grow a little louder over the coming weeks if they can keep this up.

Manchester City were turned over by Brighton to make it back-to-back league defeats

Yasin Ayari's first half goal was all that was required for Brighton to leave as the victors

Brighton's manager peeled away from the group as they enjoyed being serenaded by the away end, instead sharing a moment with match winner Yasin Ayari, whose third goal of the campaign owed much to the quick thinking of Lewis Dunk to restart play from a dead ball with haste and the individual mistake of Matheus Nunes, failing to clear Diego Gomez's cross. Ayari and Dunk were those to miss from the spot in the Carabao Cup.

'Wednesday was brutal,' Hurzeler said. 'We promised ourselves that we won't have the same feeling.

'We created energy, positivity. How the players stuck together and built the connection through the four days is really impressive.'

Hurzeler discussed the virtue of luck here in midweek and City's was out on the day, now only two points between the teams after consecutive league defeats.

The joyous, and somewhat knowing, celebrations between staff members shone a light on the preparation that went into this result and how it quite clearly serves as a warning shot.

Brighton showed across four days that they have the depth, quality and wherewithal to be at least be considered strong enough to stay close with City and Arsenal. More specifically, they showed on Saturday that they can mix the way in which they play, adept to altering circumstances.

Their full throttle movement in midfield before half time confused their City counterparts, the home midfield discombobulated – arms pointing frantically, basic organisational shouts becoming more hurried – and that filtered through to other areas of the pitch.

Maresca was seem directing Elliot Anderson on who to follow and there were occasionally some befuddled looks.

Gianluigi Donnarumma was full stretch but could do nothing about Ayari's pinpoint strike

Enzo Maresca was in disbelief as his side spurned numerous opportunities to score a goal

Out of possession, home wingers were often full backs and full backs were often stationed as wingers as they followed their men, with Brighton happily piercing through any gaps. For a while, City were taken for a ride on the waltzers.

And then later on, when City pushed and pushed, Brighton went to a back six and contained.

They still gave up a number of very presentable chances, City failing to convert five of those – most notably two for Iliman Ndiaye and Nico O'Reilly's late header – but the rearguard action is proof that they own the minerals to enjoy more days like these before May is done.

Brighton managed to create four big chances from just nine touches inside the City box, indicating that once Maresca's midfield is breached then they are too easy to play through.

The Italian – who dropped Marc Guehi - is concerned by the volume of individual mistakes at both ends of the pitch after the Nunes error.

'We're probably conceding [too many] silly goals,' Maresca said, with the defeat at Aston Villa also pockmarked by them.

'We created enough but unfortunately didn't score. For sure we are not happy. Nobody is happy when we lose. But we were aware that we weren't going to win all the games.'

Maresca said he had not reviewed two penalty appeals for handball and the decision to award a free kick in the build up to Brighton's 11th-minute goal.

Brighton showed enough quality this week to suggest they can hang with Arsenal and Man City

Man City (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma 6; Nunes 5, Khusanov 6, Dias 6, Gvardiol 5 (Foden 79); Anderson 7, Bouaddi 6 (Cherki 55, 7); Ndiaye 6 (Allan 79), Fernandez 5 (O’Reilly 65), Doku 5; Haaland 5.

Brighton (4-2-3-1): Verbruggen 7; Costinha 7, Vuskovic 7, Dunk 8, Boscagli 6 (Hadjam 64, 6); Gross 6, Chema 6 (Wieffer 64, 6); Gomez 7 (Rutter 84), Ayari 7, De Cuyper 7 (Yalcouye 72); Kostoulas 6 (Hinshelwood 72, 6).

Left back Josko Gvardiol was largely tucking in to become a third centre half and Nunes told to occupy the sort of attacking positions that the Croatian usually devours.

And interestingly, were City to win their appeal against the guilty verdicts – the sanctions for which would likely spell relegation – then left back is an area they would be expected to look at.

Sources have indicated that Bournemouth's Adrien Truffert is one potential target who was scouted extensively last season before City decided against bolstering their ranks in that area in the summer.

Rayan Ait-Nouri is looking to leave, while any signings in that position would present intrigue as to how Gvardiol and O'Reilly are used in future.

#2698. NBA fans jokingly ask why Charles Barkley ‘couldn’t cover’ US elections after Kash Patel joke

Charles Barkley made another joke about FBI Director Kash Patel on Inside the NBA, and fans think he should have been covering the elections live.

The response to Ernie Johnson's recent retirement announcement is a great example of how beloved the Inside the NBA crew is. Charles Barkley and his sense of humour are a big part of that, so of course he was going to go viral this Wednesday.

Earlier this year, Shaquille O'Neal went viral after he was named an honorary FBI Special Agent by director Kash Patel. Barkley has made jokes about it on the show this season. And another one came up, with fans taking special notice of it considering the context of the elections.

When O'Neal was being honoured by the law enforcement agency, he joked about having Barkley arrested. That is the context related to why Chuck has brought the FBI Director up multiple times already this season.

Considering the setbacks that the Republicans suffered in the midterm elections, a lot of NBA fans think Barkley's quick wit would have been amazing for covering the results in real time.

"Arguably the greatest TV hosts of all time," one fan said. "Man, CNN need them on instead of Anderson," a second fan wrote. "Nah I woulda loved to see their live reactions to the election last night," a different comment read.

"These guys should have an election night show, especially Chuck," a fourth fan wrote. "Why shouldn't they be covering the elections, Barkley is better than anyone else on TV," said a fifth fan. 'Nah man, he still got that fastball, this is too funny," a sixth fan claimed.

There is no denying that the Inside the NBA crew would be funny talking about absolutely any topic under the sun. Considering the context of the elections and all the content around them, it's not surprising to see this reaction from fans.

#2696. Matthew Stafford breaks silence on elbow injury scare with hilarious response

The last thing the Los Angeles Rams need right now is another injured superstar, especially the 38-year-old quarterback and reigning NFL MVP that is holding their Super Bowl dreams together.

So when Matthew Stafford was spotted with a bag of ice wrapped around his right throwing elbow following Sunday's victory over the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium, there was concern across the board.

Rams' head coach Sean McVay's answer when asked about it on Monday certainly didn't help extinguish the flames.

Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford answers questions after an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Chargers in Inglewood, Calif., Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. AP Photo/Caroline Brehman

"You'll have to talk to him about that," McVay said. "He's had some soreness there. I think he'd be better equipped once you guys talk to him to answer that. I can't attest to stuff that I'm not necessarily aware of."

On Wednesday, Stafford dismissed the concerns with the same casual confidence he displays while dissecting opposing defenses.

Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (9) warms up before an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Chargers in Inglewood, Calif., Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. AP Photo/Caroline Brehman

"You guys have been blind," Stafford joked. "I feel like I've been icing my arm every day out here walking around. That's on you guys."

"Listen, I'm 38 years old trying to keep up with these young bucks. A little bit of soreness and stuff that is not uncommon this time of year."

Stafford insisted his elbow hasn't affected his availability.

Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford warms up before an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Chargers in Inglewood, Calif., Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. AP Photo/Caroline Brehman

"I haven't missed a rep at practice. I haven't missed a rep in a game and I feel good. I'm not too worried about it."

That's welcome news for a Rams team whose injured reserve list is beginning to resemble a Pro Bowl roster.

Cornerback Jaylen Watson became the latest casualty Wednesday, requiring season-ending shoulder surgery. He's the third Rams player lost for the year in two weeks.

McVay acknowledged this season's injury epidemic is the worst he's experienced in 10 years, surpassing even the disastrous 2022 campaign when the defending Super Bowl champions finished 5-12.

For now, Stafford's throwing elbow appears to be one less headache for a franchise running dangerously low on healthy bodies.

#2695. Slow start dooms Cavs in 124-116 loss to the Thunder

A 17-point first-quarter deficit was too much to overcome as the Cleveland Cavaliers fell to the Oklahoma City Thunder 124 to 116, dropping to .500 with a record of 4-4.

The Cavs made a brief comeback at the start of the third quarter with an 18-3 run spanning the end of the first half and the start of the second, but could never break through. They made things interesting late with a flurry of threes, but it was too late. James Harden, who finished with 19 points, nine rebounds, and nine assists, had 10 points in the third quarter to help bring Cleveland within striking distance, but the Thunder seemingly made a play right when they needed it.

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander dominated with 42 points, four rebounds, and eight assists. Ajay Mitchell had 23 points and seven rebounds in his expanded role in the wake of key injuries to Chet Holmgren and Jalen Williams.

The Cavs were without Peyton Watson (hamstring) and Jaylon Tyson (ankle), which led to a surprise start for Tyrese Proctor. The former Duke Blue Devil contributed 11 points on 4-of-7 shooting, but limped off the court late in the fourth quarter with an ankle injury.

Donovan Mitchell tried to will the Cavs to a shocker, drilling three huge threes with just a few minutes remaining, but to no avail. Mitchell finished with 27 points and six assists, though he was on pace for another pedestrian offensive showing before catching fire in the fourth quarter.

Evan Mobley had 16 points, 10 rebounds, and three blocks, and early bright spot Mario Hezonja provided 12 points and eight rebounds off the bench. Facing a big deficit and no spark, head coach Kenny Atkinson went deep off the bench to former Cleveland State forward Tristan Enaruna in the second quarter. Some new blood helped, but the Cavs could not fully dig themselves out of the first-quarter hole.

Center Jarrett Allen suffered a knee injury in the first half and was quickly deemed doubtful to return. Allen ended up with just one rebound in seven minutes of action. Hezonja started the second half in Allen's absence.

The shorthanded Thunder were relentless, building a big lead and then holding the Cavs at arm's length the rest of the way. They had a very sloppy end to the second quarter that allowed Cleveland to crack the door open, and then came out of the half just as flat. The Cavs managed to get within seven, but never closer until late in the game.

If you only judged by the first 15 minutes of game time, the Cavs looked like a team ready to get on the flight home. But there were some good things late in the game that should give them some confidence heading into a Friday night NBA Cup showdown with LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers. Tip-off is at 7:30 at Rocket Arena.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

"He was throwing deli meat out there," Lake said. "He's seeing ghosts. I don't know what's going on, but we knew we were gonna get a couple. At least one."

On Wednesday, both Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh and Herbert himself were asked about Lake's remarks.

"As far as anybody's opinion I don't see that," Harbaugh told reporters. "Everybody's entitled to their opinion. Not what I see."

So what did Harbaugh see in the latest loss?

Herbert said he wasn't aware of Lake's comments.

"I haven't looked into it, haven't heard anything about it, so I can't really make a comment about it," Herbert told reporters. "We're really just focused on what's going on in the building, playing football and doing what we can and doing our best to, you know, go put our best effort out on Sunday. And that's all that really matters. Anything outside of that is out of our control."

Still, it's jarring to hear an NFL defender make comments about a supposed franchise quarterback that make him seem like a Jets first-round draft pick who has yet to have the game slow down. Herbert is in the seventh year of his career. He's making $52.5 million per year.

Something has happened this year. It's still not clear what it is, or whether it will change. Before it can change, the Chargers need to realize there's a problem.

And that's the most confounding part of all of it. They've lost seven and won none; at times, they sound like they've won seven and lost none.

#2685. The Daniel Jones Hate Is Just A Bit Out of Control

Hear me out, because I know even the thought of this article is going to upset a lot of people.

Daniel Jones has not played good football. I realize that. When you're the quarterback of an NFL franchise, especially on a new contract, you're paid to deliver. It's November, and the only thing he's delivered is a firesale.

I'm not naive about how bad he's been. He has 9 INTs and 2 wins, ranks 32nd in passer rating, has the second-worst TD-to-INT ratio and EPA/dropback in the league, and sits 25th in completion percentage.

But I truly believe quarterbacks get too much praise when things go well and too much blame when they don't. I'm not absolving Jones of his play, but proper criticism requires proper context, and a lot of the criticism he's getting has none.

Let's start with how the Colts built this roster in the first place.

The idea behind Jones' play last year was that he was in a better ecosystem than he had in New York. Then the Colts paid him and put him out there with ten other guys who now look a lot like what he had with the Giants. Why are we so surprised?

Heading into the year, the Colts were essentially running it back on offense, swapping out Pittman and Braden Smith for Keenan Allen and Jalen Travis. Shouldn't be too bad, right? Well, it has been.

Without AD Mitchell, there was no depth on the roster, and the Alec Pierce injury proved devastating. Josh Downs was supposed to soften the blow by playing more in heavier personnel looks. Obviously, that hasn't worked out.

Not to make this about Downs, but when you give up on highly talented WRs, do a lackluster job replenishing the room, and bet on guys to take on expanded roles they probably were never suited for, this is what happens.

Base to 11 is a major part of what's plaguing the Colts at the moment. What is Base to 11? When the Colts come out in three WR sets or 11 personnel, defenses are leaving their base defense on the field.

Why would they do that? They don't respect the speed of the offense. Why bring out more corners if you know none of these WRs are going to run by you. We can just leave bigger bodies and sell out vs. the run, because if they pass, we'll be just fine.

The Colts are battling some very complex looks that the personnel deficiencies make it impossible to overcome. Every defenses is compressed. Safeties are playing top down and nailing down on anything underneath.

In my opinion, this is the issue with the Colts right now.

They cannot pass out of these looks. They don't have enough speed on the field.

Base-to-11 and aggressive coverage techniques are one thing, but they also are consistently shooting themselves in the foot.

They are averaging 7.5 penalties a game in the last two weeks, back-to-back weeks of holding penalties negating large kickoffs and leading to backed up scenarios, missed field goals, dropped passes that turn into pick 6's.. the list really goes on.

The Colts have a laundry list of problems and the biggest indictment on Daniel Jones is that he hasn't been the solution.

He is a guy who is fighting off an Achilles issue, playing behind an offense that can't stretch a defense, and asked to carry a roster that has failed to support him at every turn.

The Colts needed a quarterback who could elevate the entire roster, and I mean elevate it to a level most teams have reached in the last five years… the postseason.

But has Daniel Jones ever been that kind QB? No. We just saw that in New York.

So why did the Colts pay him just to ask him to elevate a bad WR room, while he's coming off an achilles injury. It just doesn't make sense.

Not to mention the defense has been one of the worst in the league, if they were even league average the Daniel Jones discourse wouldn't be as loud, because the Colts would likely have more than just 2 wins.

Week after week we see defenses sell out to stop the run while Daniel Jones tries to pass his way behind the sticks in environments that aren't optimized for a QB like him to be successful.

So yes, Daniel Jones has not played good football. But if you're going to hate him for the way he's played, hate the front office first. Because I think Daniel Jones can play a lot better than he has, and maybe if he's traded he'll get a chance to show that again.

#2683. Power Rankings Roundup: 'Putrid' Cowboys slip even further heading into Week 9

That the Cowboys fell in every set of power rankings on the planet is no surprise whatsoever. But the fact that the "devastating" and "demoralizing" overtime loss to Arizona didn't drop them even further is mildly shocking. Dallas is hovering right around the fringes of the league's bottom 10 teams in the eyes of most analysts. Yet most believe the NFC East crown is still within the Cowboys' reach, partly due to the weakened state of the rest of the division, and partly because this team still has Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Quinnen Williams, Joey Porter Jr., et al.

But Week 8's collapse was simply too epic to look past with some worn-out football cliche like "any given Sunday" or "trap game" or "their guys get paid, too."

Heading into Week 9, no one is sure if the Cowboys should be buyers or sellers at the trade deadline, if a midseason coaching change is coming or not, or if the team is more likely to pack it in or go on an improbable run. But something (and maybe more than one something) feels like it has reached a breaking point at The Star. This Sunday's contest against the 2-6 Colts could determine exactly what it is.

Here's where the major outlets ranked the Cowboys at the season's halfway point and what they had to say about the NFL's most perplexing team.

On the franchise-altering Herschel Walker midseason trade in 1989: "Regardless of whether the credit for the trade goes to Jerry Jones or Jimmy Johnson, it altered the Cowboys' trajectory into becoming a three-time Super Bowl champion. They were 0-5 when they traded Walker, ending the 1989 season at 1-15. It wasn't the five players the Cowboys received from Minnesota that were important, but rather the conditional draft choices that would come if players Dallas acquired were cut the next offseason. Ultimately, the trade landed them Emmitt Smith, Kevin Smith and Darren Woodson, and gave them flexibility to make other moves. Without the trade of Walker, the Cowboys of the 1990s probably never would have existed."

"Remember when that guy in the AT&T Stadium bowels described a Cowboys loss as 'embarrassing' a few weeks ago? Well, that individual would have been spot on again on Sunday. Dallas disintegrated against the Cardinals, blowing a 17-3 lead and surrendering 467 yards to Arizona. It's a loss that feels too devastating to have occurred in Week 8. It's where the Cowboys are right now, though: They pin their hopes on their passing game, haven't improved enough defensively, and can only hope the running game produces. That's simply not a winning formula."

"The Cowboys owner said after the game, one in which Dallas blew a 24-10 lead in the final 11 minutes, that he doesn't expect to make a head coaching change during the season, but he didn't rule out doing something. 'This is something we will take a good hard look at,' Jones said. 'That was a total team effort out there for us. We have to be, for our fans, better than that.' Dallas has lost three of its last four."

"What in the hell was that against the Cardinals? That's the kind of loss that gets a coach fired. Jerry Jones said it's not happening now, but Brian Schottenheimer better get it going."

"At some point the Cowboys need to have an honest conversation about themselves, which seems impossible after team owner Jerry Jones proclaimed everyone is letting head coach Brian Schottenheimer down. Jones has talked about making big trades, and already made one in-season for cornerback Joey Porter Jr. A putrid defense that let Gardner Minshew tear it apart in the fourth quarter and overtime on Sunday needs a lot of help. But, is a team that has losses at home to a Buccaneers team led by an undrafted rookie quarterback and to a Cardinals team that came back from a 14-point deficit in the fourth quarter really a defensive piece away from contending for a Super Bowl? Probably not. It puts the Cowboys in a weird place. They're not out of the NFC East race because the division isn't good. They're also not very good themselves. It's not even outlandish for the Cowboys to look in the mirror after that hideous loss to the Cardinals and admit they should be sellers. That would require self-awareness, which isn't abundant in Dallas."

"They had been 69-0 at home when nursing a lead of at least 14 points in the fourth quarter … but that was before Sunday."

"TEASER: Stay tuned to the social accounts of MMQB podcast co-hosts Albert Breer and myself [Conor Orr] for my uber-creative solution to fixing the Cowboys defense. I think I can make it work."

"Sunday's home loss to Arizona dealt another significant blow to the Cowboys' playoff hopes. Dallas had a 14-point lead in the third quarter and again in the fourth. However, its defense, which is again one of the worst in the NFL, had no answers after Arizona made a quarterback change. The Cardinals scored touchdowns while the Cowboys settled for field goals down the stretch, and the result was a demoralizing overtime loss at home. Franchise owner Jerry Jones told reporters after the game that he won't make a coaching change during the season. If something significant doesn't change soon, though, he will be evaluating a third straight losing season."

Todd is on X at @ToddBrock24f7. Also, follow Cowboys Wire on Facebook to join in on the conversation with fellow fans!

#2682. NHL Power Rankings: Flyers flounder to start new season as Rick Tocchet searches for answers

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

I hate to get so negative just one week into the season, but the Philadelphia Flyers have forced my hand. After a magical run to the second round of the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, the Flyers have fallen on their face through four games.

Philadelphia opened the season with a 7-0 loss to the rival Pittsburgh Penguins, and coach Rick Tocchet described his team's play as "disturbing." There was only one way for the season to go after that, right? Wrong.

The Flyers are off to an 0-2-2 start, and the underlying numbers aren't pretty. Per Natural Stat Trick, they have a five-on-five expected goals share of 26.0%, which ranks last in the NHL. Their 4.57 xGA/60 also ranks last. Their 1.94 xGF/60? You guessed it. Last.

Tocchet's bunch entered the season with a lot of well-earned optimism. Even with subpar play from Matvei Michkov last season, the Flyers managed to reach the Eastern Conference Semifinals. Rookie Porter Martone asserted himself as a budding star with six goals and nine assists in 19 games between the regular season and playoffs.

There's still plenty of time -- 80 games exactly -- for the Flyers to get back on track and restore that optimism, but to say this has been a discouraging start would be an understatement.
