#2555. MLB proposes delaying salary cap in new negotiations as Dec. 1 CBA expiration inches nearer

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Major League Baseball has proposed delaying the implementation of a salary cap/floor system until 2028 as part of its latest collective bargaining agreement proposal, the league announced Tuesday. MLB says the delay is intended to provide a "smoother transition" to a salary cap/floor system and give teams more time to prepare and get their payrolls in order.

"We recognize that clubs will need a full offseason to prepare to operate within the cap and floor system. Therefore, with this offseason already underway, we proposed today to begin the cap and floor system in 2028," MLB spokesman Glen Caplin said in a statement. "This proposal would allow a smoother transition into the cap and floor system without delaying key player benefits, including earlier free agency, a $1 million minimum salary, a 30% increase to the pre-arbitration bonus pool, and transactional reform that will reduce roster churn."

The league also newly proposed a $180.2 million salary floor and a $258.2 million salary cap. Those numbers are up from $171.2 million and $245.3 million, respectively, in the league's previous proposal in June. The $1 million minimum salary would only apply to players with at least two years of service time. The minimum salary would be $900,000 for all other players.

Four teams currently have more than $258.2 million on the books for 2027 (including arbitration projections) and 20 teams have less than $180.2 million on the books, according to FanGraphs' calculations. The current competitive balance tax and revenue sharing system would remain in place in 2027 before the transition to a salary cap/floor system in 2028.

The collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1, and the owners are expected to lock out the players at that time. The previous lockout ended on March 10, then there was a three-week spring training leading up to Opening Day. If there is a similarly lengthy lockout, it would be impossible for clubs to become salary cap-compliant in such a short period of time.

The MLB Players Association has repeatedly insisted it will not accept a salary cap/floor system, and has instead proposed a revised revenue sharing system that would funnel more money from big-market teams to small-market teams. In a statement following the league's proposal on Tuesday, the MLBPA accused owners of continuing to "propose blowing up the current system and replacing it with one designed to line their pockets and increase their franchise values." The union also said that even with a delayed implementation, the league's proposal of a salary cap maintains the same "negative impacts," including a "massive reduction in player compensation" and the "elimination of fundamental player rights, including guaranteed contracts."

MLB says its push for a salary cap/floor system is intended to improve competitive balance. The small-market Milwaukee Brewers defeated the small-market Tampa Bay Rays in the World Series last week and swept big-market teams (Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Yankees) en route to the Fall Classic.

#2554. Brandon Aiyuk files to be reinstated, will report to 49ers facility this week, per report

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is taking the steps necessary to return to the field. This week, ESPN reported he had hired agent Drew Rosenhaus to represent him, and now, he has reportedly turned in paperwork filing to be reinstated. Adam Schefter says Aiyuk will report to the 49ers' facilities on Friday.

"Brandon is healthy and ready to get back on the field," Rosenhaus said.

If Aiyuk is reinstated, the 49ers could trade or release him. General manager John Lynch said 10 months ago it was safe to say the wide receiver had played his last snap for the 49ers. The franchise would like to pick up some compensation in parting ways with their two-year-old headache, but it remains to be seen if any team would offer anything for him. ESPN reported that if Aiyuk is reinstated, the most likely outcome is the franchise releasing him.

This strange saga began when Aiyuk tore his ACL in October 2024. He was placed on the PUP list prior to the 2025 season as he continued to rehab, but 13 months after his injury, it was reported that the 49ers had voided the $27 million of 2026 salary guarantees in his contract. Aiyuk apparently had not been checking in with the team, sticking to his rehab schedule or doing what his contract required of him. Aiyuk was placed on the reserve/left squad list in December.

Aiyuk spent this past offseason taking shots at the 49ers on social media, and acting as if he were going to reunite with his college quarterback in Jayden Daniels and sign with the Washington Commanders. However, the 49ers still owned his rights, so Aiyuk had to file for reinstatement and then be acquired via trade if his Washington dream were to come true. Aiyuk refused to complete these steps in the offseason, but now, he's playing ball.

Aiyuk established himself as one of the best wide receivers in the NFL in 2023, as he caught 75 passes for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns on the way to Super Bowl LVIII. His 3.1 yards per route run that year ranked No. 3 behind Tyreek Hill and Nico Collins, and his 81.3% of receptions going for a first down or a touchdown ranked first in the NFL.

The offseason following the Super Bowl appearance, Aiyuk orchestrated a "hold-in" during training camp, which eventually led to the four-year, $120 million extension he was after. That 2024 season, Aiyuk reached 50 yards receiving in just one of the seven games he played in before tearing his ACL.

#2553. NBA Bracketology: Projecting the full 20-team postseason field as Knicks, Thunder take steps back

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The NBA comes at you fast. One moment the Knicks are riding high off their first championship in 53 years, the next they're off to a sluggish start and scrambling to recover from losing their first three games. The Thunder went into the season rightly hailed as one of the deepest teams in the NBA — then had that assumption tested in harsh fashion after sustaining injuries to three of their five starters, with Jalen Williams (ankle and fibula) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) expected to miss most, if not all, of the season, and Chet Holmgren (knee) out at least two months.

While OKC suffered the most brutal blows on the injury front, the Thunder are hardly alone there. Several big name stars have already gone down and missed multiple games, among them Anthony Edwards (knee), Kawhi Leonard (knee), Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring), Jalen Duren (hamstring), Paolo Banchero (ankle), Jaren Jackson Jr (knee) and Ja Morant (hamstring).

The net effect is that an NBA season that was already expected to be competitive and wide open — particularly in the East, where the conference is as deep as it's been in recent memory — has been thrown into flux. While the Spurs and Thunder remain the betting favorites to win it all, the Sixers, Knicks, Celtics, Rockets, Raptors and Timberwolves are bunched up right behind them, with the Nuggets, Pistons, Cavaliers, Lakers and Blazers not far behind.

In the actual standings, the new-look Sixers have won seven of their first eight and are perched atop the Eastern Conference, while the surprising Memphis Grizzlies got out to a hot start in the West and were the last team in the league to lose their first game after getting upended by the Pelicans in overtime at home on Monday night. Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Heat are under .500 and still trying to figure it out, while the Wolves and Warriors are just two teams out of several trying to stay afloat until key members of their respective teams return to the floor.

Various prediction models have differing opinions on what all this means in the long run. Those forecasts vary wildly, with one favoring the Raptors to come out of the East and another giving four other teams a better shot to win the conference than Toronto.

Predicting how all this will shake out in the end is difficult at best and folly at worst — so naturally that's exactly what we'll try to do over the course of the season.

This is our first installment of semi-regular NBA seeding predictions -- the NBA version of Bracketology -- where we'll give our best guess on where teams will be slotted once the playoffs roll around. The methodology is super scientific: watch a lot of basketball, consult with the mountain of stats and data available, and then eyeball it. Your mileage may vary.

Despite Duren playing all of 38 minutes this season, the Pistons have reminded everyone why they were the top seed in the East last season and have designs on something similar again this year. Detroit has proven to be a quality regular-season team, but the Pistons are still in desperate need of more shot creators and scoring to help ease the burden on Cade Cunningham. Their front office has work to do to level up the roster and avoid another disappointing postseason.

After what could charitably be called a tumultuous offseason, the Celtics once again look like a competitive, competent organization (apart from their struggles in Houston on Monday in the second night of a back-to-back) that figures to be a tough out in the East. Jayson Tatum is playing well enough to openly wonder "why not me?" when it comes to the MVP conversation, while Paul George's numbers to start the season look a lot more like the PG we saw in his final campaign with the Clippers rather than (mercifully for him and Boston) the lackluster version who was only intermittently available during his time in Philadelphia.

There were questions about the new-look Sixers going into the season, mainly how four big-name stars in the starting lineup would co-exist. The answer to date is that they've figured out ways to win when things have sometimes looked bleak. The Sixers lead the league in clutch victories, with six of their seven wins coming in games decided by five points or fewer with under five minutes to go. More surprising: they're top five in defensive rating and have allowed the second fewest points per game.

On paper, the Knicks have the best starting five in the NBA. That hasn't changed. Even though they didn't start the season looking like the dominant version of themselves that ripped through the playoffs en route to a title, the talent in New York remains undeniable.

The Raptors were a good defensive team last year and figure to be so again, but how far Toronto goes this season will be directly tied to Kawhi's availability — something that has been largely unknowable for much of the last decade of Leonard's career. As for the Cavaliers, their starting five is among the best in the league. After that, the roster gets thin and the questions begin to mount for Kenny Atkinson and the analytics team.

Maybe this is disrespecting the Hawks by lumping them with three teams that hardly inspire confidence, but the East feels like it has a solid six and then a pretty squishy bunch jockeying for play-in positioning. Miami fans won't like being in this group either — even though members of the Heat overreacted to their ugly start just like the rest of us and wondered aloud about the floor spacing and fit between Giannis and Bam Adebayo. Banchero is once again hurt in Orlando, but even when he's healthy, he and Franz Wagner (who is still searching for his elusive 3-point shot) have achieved exactly nothing together. The Wizards have been surprisingly plucky to begin the season, but if you're skeptical about Trae Young and Anthony Davis being on the floor enough to actually influence their record and help them sneak into the play-in, you aren't alone. Feel free to swap out the Hornets for one of these last-chance slots; Charlotte has been without the services of Kon Knueppel (hamstring) thus far and would undoubtedly benefit from his return.

Not pictured: the Pacers, who will be going nowhere fast if Haliburton and Ivica Zubac (ankle) don't get back on the floor sooner than later and stay there.

The Spurs are the biggest beneficiaries of the league-wide injury virus that has yet to infect them. The defending Western Conference champs are healthy, which is more than most teams can say. They still need to figure out the crowded and sometimes clunky backcourt fit between De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper, but as long as Victor Wembanyama is available, the West is once again theirs for the taking.

The Rockets were sorely in need of guard play last season after Fred VanVleet missed the season with a knee injury. He's back, and Houston has looked stout at both ends of the floor to begin the season (including Monday evening's comfortable home win over the Celtics). But is FVV's return enough to boost the Rockets and propel them to a deep postseason run, or does Houston need to make a move in a conference that is suddenly up for grabs outside of San Antonio? There will be endless rumors between now and the trade deadline about how the Rockets could use someone like Kyrie Irving — which does not mean the Mavericks will be keen on moving him.

If there's any team that could withstand losing three of its five starters for a significant chunk of the season, it's OKC. Sam Presti has done a masterful job making the Thunder into the deepest team in the league, but this represents the biggest challenge OKC has faced since developing into a perennial contender. How much weight can Shai Gilgeous-Alexander be reasonably expected to carry, and will guys like Ajay Mitchell, Isaiah Hartenstein, Alex Caruso, Jared McCain, and rookies Aday Mara and Bennett Stirtz be able to fill the void created in the absence of Williams, Wallace and Holmgren?

Luka Dončić is off to a scorching start, leads the league in scoring and has played better defense at times (and doesn't mind saying so himself), though even JJ Redick has openly questioned the roster and what the ancillary parts can be reasonably trusted with on a nightly basis. The Nuggets are once again thin after the starting five and are heavily reliant on Nikola Jokić and Jamal Murray. And through the first five games, the Blazers boasted the third-best point differential in the league — but also lost Morant to a hamstring injury that will keep him out of the lineup for a while. At least it's Dame Time in Portland again.

There were those of us who doubted the fit with Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball and wondered whether the duo could make the Wolves into contenders — and that was before the team announced that Edwards would undergo an unexpected in-season knee surgery. That's asking Ball to do a lot in his absence. Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has played well and talked even better, but Golden State is still painfully thin while waiting for Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody to return from knee injuries (to say nothing of Kristaps Porzingis, whose status remains a mystery). Kyrie's name has been unsurprisingly floated in various trade rumors, but the Mavericks just might be competitive enough to entertain keeping him around. After moving on from Desmond Bane, Jaren Jackson Jr and Morant, the Grizzlies were supposed to be rebooting the franchise around rookie Cam Boozer. Memphis benefited mightily from a paper-thin schedule to start with wins over the Jazz (twice), Kings (twice), Warriors and Blazers before the Pelicans finally handed them their first L. It only gets harder from here — but even qualifying for the play-in would represent a successful season in Memphis.

#2552. Bruno Fernandes holds back TEARS after Man United beaten by Chelsea: Captain appears emotional as return to squad after public criticism of Michael Carrick ends in defeat

Published: 16:49 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 19:55 EDT, 31 October 2026

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes appeared to be on the verge of tears as he embraced the travelling faithful following his side's latest defeat.

Fernandes returned to the United side after being dropped for their loss against Bournemouth last week, when he was an unused substitute.

The decision from Michael Carrick came after his skipper had criticised Carrick's tactics in the 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, leading to uncertainty around the duo's relationship.

In the week, however, they held crisis talks to fix their relationship, and Fernandes was back in the team – and playing 90 minutes – against Chelsea on Saturday.

Yet he was unable to turn around his side's fortunes, with United falling to a 2-0 defeat, and the club have now gone nine games in all competitions without a win.

And he appeared to be in a battle to hold back the tears as United's players headed over to the away end at full-time, showing how much the team's poor form is affecting him.

A visibly emotional Bruno Fernandes after another disappointing result for Man Utd 💔 pic.twitter.com/E4MhUoD8VW

Bruno Fernandes appeared to be fighting back the tears following Manchester United's defeat by Chelsea

Carrick has made a habit of applauding the fans first after the game, and was cheered off following the Bournemouth defeat before those in attendance turned on the players.

On this occasion, Carrick again walked down the tunnel without his players, but the team were in fact cheered.

Fernandes was stood alone, and repeatedly wiped his face as he took in the situation.

'He's a big player, Bruno,' Carrick said after the game. 'He offers us so much, you know, with his experience.

'He's been through a lot here and achieved a lot and shown what he can bring to the team.

'So he's an important part of the team for us and I think we've got a good balance today. We've got a good team and the boys are looking forward to it.'

#2551. Browns' Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol: Shedeur Sanders potentially in line to start Week 9 at Saints

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson entered the NFL's concussion protocol Tuesday morning, the Browns announced. Watson, who passed concussion evaluation after taking a helmet-to-helmet hit during Sunday's loss to the Steelers, told team doctors he started feeling concussion-like symptoms Monday night.

Deshaun Watson has been placed in concussion protocol pic.twitter.com/ViiyRHMct8

Should Watson be unable to play in Week 9 against the Saints, the Browns would likely turn to second-year pro Shedeur Sanders.

Watson briefly left Sunday's contest in Pittsburgh after a spotter called down to the sideline for Watson to be checked out after Jaquan Brisker's helmet-to-helmet hit (which was flagged). Sanders entered the game briefly before Watson returned. Watson finished the 27-6 loss with 324 passing yards but also eight sacks and zero touchdowns.

Brisker flagged for hit on Watson #Steelers #NFL pic.twitter.com/FCOv8QtjJA

The Browns say they also evaluated Watson for a concussion after the game and again Monday morning, per league rules. However, when Watson reported his symptoms to the team on Tuesday morning, Cleveland immediately put him in the protocol.

Sanders, 24, could start Sunday in a crucial game for the Browns, who are 5-3 this season. He has appeared in two games this year, but only for five snaps. He has completed all three of his passes for 2 yards.

Sanders did get considerable playing time as part of Cleveland's quarterback carousel last year, appearing in eight games (seven starts). He threw seven touchdown passes and 10 interceptions while completing 56.6% of his passes. He had some impressive performances, including a three-touchdown day against the Titans, but struggled overall. Out of 36 quarterbacks with at least 200 pass attempts, he was last in completion percentage, touchdown-to-interception rate and passer rating.

Sanders lost the quarterback battle to Watson this offseason, but should he be called upon to start, he'd be in a much better offensive ecosystem than he was in last year. The Browns have upgraded their offensive line and wide receivers, with rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion impressing. The Saints could potentially provide a soft landing spot, too: New Orleans' defense ranks 28th in both yards per play and yards per game.

#2550. Ty Jerome is on a Linsanity-esque run, but here's why his MVP-level scoring isn't that big of a surprise

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Memphis Grizzlies finally lost a game on Monday night, their first of the year. But, of course, Ty Jerome was still the story. The Grizzlies point guard, who has gone full Linsanity Mode to start the season, rattled off 40 points on 64% shooting against the Pelicans. He made five of his six 3-pointers. He made seven of his eight free throws.

With the Grizzlies trailing 124-115 at the 1:43 mark, Jerome engineered a personal 9-0 run to close regulation and send the game to overtime.

TY JEROME HEATER TO FORCE OT!!! pic.twitter.com/kmet2W6esv

Less than two weeks removed from opening night (when Jerome put 45 on the Jazz), it's obviously too early to have a real MVP discussion. But, if we could, Jerome would be in it. The league's sixth-leading scorer, he's now averaging 28.3 points per game on 50/42/88 shooting splits.

People are wondering: how is this possible? Wasn't this guy a G League player? Yes, he was. But that was five years ago, and if you've been paying attention, you know he's been making consistent leaps as he has earned more and more opportunities. It's not to say anyone could've seen this kind of scoring boom coming, but there were signs.

Agfter bumping around with the Suns, Thunder and Warriors through the first four years of his career, Jerome, who had played well with whatever time he got specifically in OKC and Golden State, broke out with the Cavs during the 2024-25 season. He averaged 12.5 PPG on 51/44 shooting splits, finished third in Sixth Man of the Year voting, and became a legit go-to scorer in the playoffs.

In Clevaland's first-round sweep over the Heat, Jerome averaged over 16 PPG, making 10 of his 20 3-pointers and shooting 51% overall. In Game 1, he scored 16 of his 28 points on 6-of-7 shooting in the fourth quarter.

Look deeper at that season, and you'll see that Jerome was an All-Star-level scorer relative to his playing time, averaging 22.7 points per 36 minutes. That was a better mark that Jamal Murray, Tyrese Haliburton and Jimmy Butler, among many others. The only reason he wasn't a 20 PPG scorer was he only played 19.9 minutes per night on a Cleveland team that had Donovan Mitchell and Darius Garland ahead of him.

The Grizzlies saw this, and in the summer of 2025 signed Jerome to a three-year, $28 million contract that now looks like the biggest non-rookie bargain in the league. He only played in 15 games last season, but once again he was a per-minute monster.

After missing the first three-plus months to a calf strain, Jerome scored 20 points in 20 minutes in his Grizzlies debut, and over the following six weeks he averaged 0.87 points per minute played, the same mark as Kawhi Leonard and fourth-best in the league among players who logged at least 10 games.

The evidence was clear: If Jerome is on the court, he's going to score. It's just a matter of playing time. So far this season, he's playing 30 minutes per night, and is currently scoring 0.91 points in each of those minutes. That registers as the fourth-best mark in the league among players who have played at least 100 minutes.

It's not to say we should've seen an MVP-level start coming for Jerome, but at the same time this scoring wave he's currently riding didn't come out of nowhere. The signs trace back to Cleveland. As his minutes, and usage, have gone up, so too has his scoring. He is simply playing more minutes now with a 31.3% usage rate equal to Jalen Brunson.

Again, that's not to say Jerome is a superstar. But don't be thrown off by his underdog story or his lack of NBA athleticism. He's extraordinarily skilled and always has been. He's a world-class shooter, both off the catch and dribble, near and far. Going back to Cleveland, he has consistently ranked north of the 90th percentile as both a pick-and-roll and isolation scorer, per Synergy. What he's doing to start this season probably won't continue, but it also didn't come out of nowhere.

#2549. Stuttgart left frustrated in Istanbul as Batrakov double proves costly

A ferocious atmosphere greeted Stuttgart at RAMS Park, with Atakan Karazor picking up a yellow card inside the opening minute after catching Mario Lemina in midfield.

But, despite the hosts' early intensity, it would be the visitors who almost took the lead in the eighth minute. Chris Führich and Maximilian Mittelstädt combined well down the left to find Jamie Leweling, whose effort remarkably struck both posts before bouncing clear.

Galatasaray then made the visitors pay four minutes later, as Jeff Chabot's attempted clearance fell to Aleksey Batrakov just to the right of the penalty spot, before the Russian fired past Fabian Bredlow, who got a strong hand to the ball and should perhaps have done better.

Just three minutes later, Batrakov had his second, latching onto a pass from Davinson Sánchez before slipping the ball through Bredlow's legs to double Galatasaray's advantage.

Stuttgart's miserable opening continued when Karazor was forced off through injury, with youngster Yanik Spalt coming on in his place, before Galatasaray nearly added a third in the 22nd minute, with Bredlow denying Batrakov his hat-trick and Viktor Osimhen firing the rebound over the crossbar.

Tempers flared with around ten minutes remaining before the break, as Barış Alper Yılmaz sent Führich tumbling off the pitch, sparking a confrontation involving players and members of both coaching staffs.

Führich, heavily involved throughout the half, came close to pulling one back in the 42nd minute, curling an effort toward the far corner after cutting inside Roland Sallai, only for Uğurcan Çakır to get a slight touch and turn the ball narrowly wide.

In the second half, the intensity from the visitors increased, with Führich continuing to have a superb game down the left for VfB.

Seeking control again, Galatasaray turned to Rafa Leao for their own energy on their respective left flank, but it was Stuttgart who remained in the ascendancy.

The biggest moment yet for Die Schwaben came just after 75 minutes, when Deniz Undav rattled the bar from the middle of the box, before Führich found the net from range with a curling effort.

However, the Stuttgart hope would be short-lived, with referee Chris Kavanagh announcing that the goal had been ruled out for offside against skipper Undav.

Undav would remain at the heart of things for the visitors, sending Dženan Pejčinović through on goal in the 86th minute, before the summer signing failed to beat Çakır inside the box, as his wait for a goal outside of the DFB-Pokal goes on, rather summing up the frustrating evening for Stuttgart.

And after all of that, it ended 2-0 to Galatasaray, who had to hold on at times in the second half, but were more than worth the three points after such a threatening first-half performance.

Now, Stuttgart turn their attention to Saturday's clash with Bremen, while they have to wait until the end of the month for their next Champions League clash, when they travel to Inter Milan on 25 November.

#2548. Jadeveon Clowney mock trades: Cowboys reunion headlines four deals Texans can make before NFL trade deadline

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

With the NFL trade deadline less than a week away, the hot stove is officially boiling. More and more names are being bandied about with each passing day. Some of them are big and some are smaller, but it seems like things could get pretty wild ahead of Nov. 10.

One name that has been floated in recent days is Houston Texans edge rusher Jadeveon Clowney. ESPN reported earlier this week that the former No. 1 overall pick's name has surfaced in trade discussions.

The Texans are sitting at 2-3, three full games back of the Jacksonville Jaguars in the AFC South and 2.5 games back of the final wild card spot. Clowney himself has played sparingly, appearing on only 37% of Houston's defensive snaps so far this season. He's also been fairly unproductive, recording just 1.5 sacks, two tackles for loss and four quarterback hits.

His pressure rate of 13.0%, though, indicates he's been a bit more effective than his counting stats, as he ranks 58th out of 262 players who have rushed the passer at least 50 times so far this season, according to Tru Media. The sample is very small, as Clowney has just 69 pass-rush snaps.

Still, given Clowney's age (33 years old) and relative lack of production, it's hard to see him generating much in the way of a trade return for the Texans. It's most likely that he would net a late-round pick at most, and perhaps only a swap of picks. The Texans sent one of their 2027 seventh-round picks to Cleveland in 2025 and another to Detroit this past offseason in the David Montgomery deal, but have one incoming from the Chargers, so that is the pick we have them sending out in each deal.

As for a few teams that could make sense for Clowney, here's a list.

The Niners have already given their defensive line a boost by trading for DeForest Buckner, and they should welcome Nick Bosa back into the fold soon, if not this week coming off their bye. But they're still just 21st in the NFL in pressure rate, according to Tru Media, and they have been dealing with injuries along the defensive front all season. Adding another capable rotational player off the edge could give them an extra boost ahead of a potential playoff run.

The Chiefs have bigger needs, with the most obvious one being wide receiver, but that doesn't mean they can't use at least some help in the pass rush department. George Karlaftis has 34 pressures this season, but R Mason Thomas, Felix Anudike-Uzomah and Ashton Gillotte have combined for only 42, according to Pro Football Focus. Adding another body to the mix could have some merit. The Chiefs have a 2027 sixth-round pick incoming from the 49ers, likely very late in the round, which they can send out here.

To be clear, the Cowboys should almost certainly not be buyers ahead of the deadline. They are 3-5 and going nowhere fast. But we know that Jerry Jones doesn't operate that way. He fears irrelevance more than anything else, and the Cowboys are in danger of becoming irrelevant this season. Clowney was in Dallas last year and racked up 8.5 sacks but the team elected not to re-sign him because of scheme fit concerns, but with the pass rush mostly not getting home, perhaps the Cowboys would bring him back. Dallas sends out a 2028 pick here because the 2027 sixth-rounder is headed to Pittsburgh in the Joey Porter Jr. trade.

The Giants are in first place in the NFC East and apparently going hunting for all kinds of players at the deadline. With Brian Burns out for the year, the Giants check in 31st in pressure rate, per Tru Media, and they could use some help for Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux coming off the edge. If they allocate more resources to other positions, it could make sense to go for a cheaper option on the defensive front. The Giants have an incoming sixth-round pick in the 2027 draft from the Jacksonville Jaguars, and that's likely to land pretty late in the round.

#2547. NBA Power Rankings: Warriors fly into top 10 with rejuvenated Stephen Curry, 76ers pushing for top spot

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

After the Warriors' win over Phoenix on Monday, their fifth straight (something they never managed last season), Stephen Curry was asked what about this year's squad feels different from the one that finished with 37 wins a year ago.

"I mean, Yax," Curry laughed, stating the obvious when it comes to the historic start of Warriors' rookie Yaxel Lendeborg. "BP [Brandin Podziemski] taking another step forward. B-Will [Brandon Williams] has been great for us off the bench, giving us something we haven't had in a while. We've had some individual production that's been pretty cool, some standout guys who've made their presence felt night after night.

"But I think collectively," Curry continued, "we're probably a little bit more prepared on the details of what we're trying to do, and not just taking for granted that you can just play like the Warriors of old and expect good things to happen."

Curry didn't elaborate on these "details" on which the Warriors are more focused this season, but it looks about the same on the statistical surface. They're playing at the same pace. Making the same amount of 3s. They're still a high-turnover offense. They remain small, collectively old and not particularly athletic. They own a nearly identical 114-ish defensive rating, which at the moment has them ranked as a bottom-10 unit. Their spot-up, pick-and-roll, transition and isolation frequencies are all pretty much the same, per Synergy.

Which is to say, the Warriors are, in fact, playing like the Warriors. They look so good, that they've jumped 15 spots this week into the top 10 of our weekly NBA Power Rankings. Let's break down three reasons why.

Anyone who says they can see slippage in Curry's game must be looking through one hell of a high-powered microscope. He's scoring more than a point a minute (30 PPG in 28.8 MPG). The only other player doing that, with at least 100 minutes played, is Luka Dončić.

Get this: According to Cleaning the Glass, the 137.4 points that Curry is currently scoring per 100 shot attempts registers as a career high. He's taking more than 10 3-pointers a night and connecting at a 43% clip. On Monday, he finally missed a free throw after making 51 straight to start the year.

So yeah, Curry is still Curry. The difference is, he's got a real co-star again (remember, this team was tracking toward a conference finals trip when Jimmy Butler first came over) in the form a 24-year-old rookie.

Even knowing Curry's greatness, just about everyone pegged Golden State as a lottery team this year. They may still end up there, but at the moment Lendeborg has completely revived a team that we had all left for dead. He's the only rookie in history other than Larry Bird to post at least 100 points, 40 rebounds and 20 assists through his first five games. He's just the third player in Warriors history to average north of 20 PPG (22.3) over his first seven games of his career, joining Wilt Chamberlain and Rick Barry. In the win over the Clippers on Sunday, he became the fourth rookie in history log a game with at least 37 points and five assists on 85% true shooting.

Lendeborg is tracking toward Rookie of the Year and honest All-Star consideration. He has given the Warriors a legit first option without Curry on the court, and, in tandem, he massively eases Curry's burden as a creator. The guy is already a pick-and-roll machine and, at the moment, the most efficient isolation scorer in the league.

For some reason Podziemski has become a punching bag for a lot of Warriors fans, but he's been a winning player from day one (just go look at his on/off splits dating back to his rookie year). With Butler out, and until Lendeborg came along, Podziemski was the only Warrior other than Curry who could generate real paint pressure.

This season, Podziemski is putting it all together to the tune of a career-high 17 points, five assists and five boards per game. Once again, the splits tell the tale: The Warriors have outscored opponents by 50 points with Podziemski on the floor so far this year, by far the team high.

Suddenly the Warriors have three to four guys on any given night who can break a defense down, and with that you're seeing these support-staff guys like Georges Niang, Gui Santos, De'Anthony Melton, Gary Payton II, Will Richard, Al Horford, and even Charles Bassey (who has gone from taking DNPs to putting up 25 points and 18 boards over the last two games) to ride shotgun on a top-five offense.

And now for the rest of the Power Rankings:

#2546. Ravens trade candidates: Three quarterbacks Baltimore should consider amid injury crisis

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Baltimore Ravens sit in a dangerous position, as they lost their top two quarterbacks to injury, and their third option is also questionable. On his first passing attempt in the eventual 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills, Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury that required surgery, landed him on injured reserve and could end his season. Then, Tyler Huntley suffered a season-ending turf toe injury as well.

That forced undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into the lineup, who completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and one interception vs. Buffalo. However, he's nursing an ankle injury and is considered questionable for the Ravens' Week 9 matchup vs. the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday. That led Baltimore to add Kedon Slovis and Austin Reed to its roster.

While Fagnano will likely join Anthony Brown as the only undrafted rookie quarterbacks to start a game for the Ravens, should the team consider chasing a legitimate starter prior to next Tuesday's trade deadline? While Baltimore does reside in last place in the division with a 4-4 record, the season isn't over yet. Let's examine three quarterback options for the Ravens to consider.

The Arizona Cardinals demoted Jacoby Brissett from starter to third-stringer this week, as Mike LaFleur is moving forward with Gardner Minshew and rookie Carson Beck as his new No. 2. Brissett was benched for Minshew in the third quarter of the Cardinals' Week 8 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys, who sparked the offense with three touchdown passes in the fourth quarter to get the game to overtime. The Cardinals won that game in the extra period, leading LaFleur to make the decision he did.

Brissett has not been terrible this season. He's completed 63.3% of his passes for 1,719 yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions in eight games. His 75.6 yards per game to Trey McBride entering Week 8 were the most by a QB-TE combo since 1970 (min. 15 games). Brissett isn't going to be raking in Pro Bowl votes, but he's a borderline starter in this league that would be an upgrade over an undrafted rookie or career third-stringer.

This would be the most intriguing swing of the bat for general manager Eric DeCosta, as Anthony Richardson is the option that offers the most upside. The former No. 4 overall pick out of Florida hasn't made a start since 2024, but he's one of the most athletic quarterback prospects we've ever seen. Obviously, it hasn't gone according to plan for him with the Indianapolis Colts. The 24-year-old quarterback is 8-7 as a starter, having completed 50.9% of his passes with 11 touchdowns and 13 interceptions in 18 total games played. Availability and consistency have been major issues for Richardson, but a change of scenery could do wonders for him.

Before you write Richardson off as a complete bust, consider the impact J.J. McCarthy is having early on for the New York Giants. Why couldn't Richardson thrive after his long-awaited trade? Plus, Richardson is a dual-threat athlete who could pair well with Derrick Henry. He averaged 40 rushing yards per game in his first two seasons, and scored 10 touchdowns on the ground as well. Give me the read option every play.

Tyson Bagent of the Chicago Bears has been floated as a trade candidate for the Ravens given his familiarity with new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle. Bagent has truly been one of the most fascinating stories we've seen in the NFL over the past couple of seasons. Undrafted in 2023 out of Shepherd University -- a Division II school in Shepherdstown, West Virginia, Bagent did enough with Chicago in his first preseason to earn a spot on the final 53-man roster. As a rookie, he was called upon to make four starts, and even defeated No. 1 overall pick Bryce Young and the Carolina Panthers in prime time.

Bagent signed a two-year, $10 million extension in 2025, but has struggled this season. He threw for 268 yards and one interception in the Week 4, 23-12 win against the New York Jets, then threw for just 87 yards and two interceptions in the 31-7 blowout loss suffered at the hands of the Green Bay Packers the following week. Bagent's struggles look even worse considering that 38-year-old Case Keenum threw for 247 yards and two touchdowns in a primetime upset of the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 3. If Caleb Williams had to miss another start at some point, you have to wonder who Ben Johnson would start at quarterback this time around.

One question to consider is what would the Bears want for Bagent? If Ryan Poles wants a fourth-round pick for him,it should be "thanks but no thanks."

#2545. MLB offseason bold predictions: Tarik Skubal breaks records, World Series champ gets a deal, a FA frenzy, more

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

With the Brewers crowned World Series champions, the 2026-27 offseason is underway. We're still waiting for the first significant free agent signing or trade, which isn't unusual less than a week into the offseason. Give it another week or so and the action will pick up. Before the hot stove really gets burning, here are 10 bold predictions for the 2026-27 offseason. Remember, all geniuses were called crazy at first.

Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million deal with the Dodgers is the largest pitching contract in history, and our first bold prediction says Tarik Skubal, this offseason's undisputed No. 1 free agent, will beat that. Specifically, he'll sign a contract that is closer to $400 million in value than $300 million, which is another way of saying he'll clear $350 million and break Yamamoto's record for total dollars by a good bit. Scott Boras, Skubal's agent, likes to break contract records with room to spare, not just by a tiny bit. Skubal is the best free agent starter since Yamamoto, and the best free agent starter with MLB experience since Gerrit Cole in 2019. It's a very thin free agent class with few places to (wisely) spend money. The bet here is a team steps up and gives Skubal a record deal.

Milwaukee's thing over the last few years has been trading its top players a year before free agency (Corbin Burnes, Freddy Peralta, Devin Williams, etc.) and obviously it has worked for them. William Contreras is at that point now: he's scheduled to hit the open market next offseason. This next bold prediction says the Brewers will buck that trend and instead sign the World Series MVP to a long-term extension that keeps him in Milwaukee for at least another few years, if not the rest of his career. How does six years at $24 million a pop sound? That would be $144 million total and the richest contract given to a catcher in the last 13 years, clearing Will Smith's $140 extension with the Dodgers. The World Series champs keep their most irreplaceable player. It has been foretold.

Every offseason is important, and this one is extra important for new Astros GM Randy Flores, who must figure out what to do with third baseman Isaac Paredes and shortstop Jeremy Peña, both a year away from free agency. Keeping Peña and trading Paredes, and installing Carlos Correa at the hot corner, is the sensible move. This bold prediction says the opposite will happen. The Astros will trade Peña and keep Paredes, and figure out their 2027 infield alignment later. Houston needs help up and down the roster, particularly on the mound, and I think the offers for Peña will simply be too great for Flores to ignore. It will be similar to the Kyle Tucker trade two years ago. The Astros don't have to move Peña, but the offers will get to a point where they just can't say no.

On one hand, keeping the offense intact and adding some pitching would be a viable offseason plan for the Braves. On the other hand, can they really run it back with the same offense that flatlined after June 1 and in the NLDS? It might be time to shake things up a bit, and I boldly predict it will happen. Ronald Acuña Jr., Drake Baldwin, Michael Harris II, and Matt Olson aren't going anywhere. No team will take the current version of Austin Riley and the six years (!) remaining on his contract. That leaves Ozzie Albies and I suppose Sean Murphy, though the latter is well into role player status now. Does that make this bold prediction a "the Braves will trade Albies" prediction? Yeah, I guess it does. It feels like things are getting a little stale in Atlanta and it's time to change up a core.

You could argue Freddy Peralta is the second-best free agent starter behind Skubal. You could also argue it's Trevor Rogers, who doesn't have Peralta's pedigree or track record, but has strong under-the-hood performance indicators, the kind that project well into the future and get players paid. So, for this bold prediction, I'll say that Rogers signs a richer deal than Peralta, even though the latter is the more famous player and has been better in their careers to date. It'll be close. I can see Rogers getting something in the $125 million range and Peralta signing for right around $120 million, but, in the end, Rogers will sign for more guaranteed dollars because he's a year and a half younger and teams love nothing more than players they believe have untapped upside. That's Rogers, not Peralta.

After the Dodgers swept in the NLCS, there were calls to infuse some youth into the roster, and, honestly, they need it. Fortunately, Los Angeles has one of the best prospects in the game in the precocious Josue De Paula, who was so impressive late in the season. Trading an outfielder to clear a spot for De Paula seems like such an obvious move that I'm not sure this prediction qualifies as bold. Andy Pages and Kyle Tucker aren't going anywhere, which leaves Teoscar Hernández. How about a trade that sends Hernández back to the Blue Jays? It's a one-year commitment, the Blue Jays badly need over-the-fence power, and the fan base already loves the guy. Teoscar to Toronto as what amounts to their George Springer replacement. I boldly predict it.

Every offseason, there are two teams that appear to match up so well that a trade feels inevitable. Last offseason, it was the Brewers and Mets for a Freddy Peralta deal. This offseason, it's the Cubs and Yankees. The Cubs need rotation help and have some young position players to spare (like Matt Shaw). The Yankees need infield help and have starting pitching to trade (like Will Warren). I'm not saying Shaw for Warren will happen or even should happen. I'm just saying Chicago's and New York's trade chips and roster needs align very well, and when that happens, a trade typically comes together. This bold prediction says the Cubs will send a position player to the Yankees for a starting pitcher, with maybe some other pieces involved on both sides.

There are trade rumors involving a Mariners starting pitcher every offseason and there's a good reason for that. They have a lot of really good starters and teams want them. The Mariners currently have Kade Anderson, Logan Gilbert, Emerson Hancock, George Kirby, Bryce Miller, and Bryan Woo lined up for their 2027 rotation. They could keep them all because pitching depth has a way of disappearing, sure, but Seattle needed another bat even before Randy Arozarena became a free agent. This next bold prediction says the Mariners finally trade one of their starters in an arm-for-bat deal. I'll say Kirby, who is two years away from free agency, is the one to go. Gilbert is a one-year rental but the better pitcher. The others all have longer control than Kirby.

After coming out of the gate so well in April and May, Munetaka Murakami finished right where the pundits expected. He hit .207 and had the highest strikeout rate among qualified hitters, but he also slugged 35 home runs in only 127 games. Hanshin Tigers third baseman Teruaki Sato, who will be posted for MLB teams this offseason, is similar to Murakami as a strikeout-prone lefty with huge power. This bold prediction says Sato will double Murakami's contract with the White Sox (two years and $34 million) because he's a better bet to stay at third base, a position that is barren in free agency, and because Murakami provided proof of concept. He showed that a player with big contact concerns in Japan can indeed succeed stateside, even if it is an eyesore at times. Four years and $68 million for Sato, perhaps with an opt out that makes the $68 million not really $68 million.

Dec. 1 is of course when the collective bargaining agreement expires and the owners are expected to lock out the players. My final bold prediction says free agents and teams will get out ahead of the potential lockout and sign in November. Players won't want to wait until who knows when to sign and teams will want to lock in contracts so they can be grandfathered into whatever the next CBA brings. MLB free agency tends to be slow-moving. Last offseason, only one of our top 10 free agents signed in November, and that was Shota Imanaga taking the qualifying offer. Only three other top 10 free agents signed in December. The other six signed on Jan. 14 or later. This offseason will be the opposite, I boldly predict. There will be a flurry of activity in November and at least seven of our top 10 free agents will put pen to paper before a potential lockout.

#2544. Robert Kraft named one of five contributor nominees for 2027 Pro Football Hall of Fame class

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Patriots owner Robert Kraft is one of five contributor nominees for the 2027 Pro Football Hall of Fame class, it was announced Wednesday. The Contributor Subcommittee whittled the field down from 42 options to five, and it will meet again on Nov. 17 to decide on one of the five remaining nominees to advance to the full Selection Committee. The Selection Committee will then announce its selections for the 2027 class shortly before the Super Bowl.

Kraft is joined by Ralph Hay, Virginia McCaskey, Doug Williams and John Wooten.

Kraft received the subcommittee's vote last year to advance to the Selection Committee vote, but he was controversially left out of the 2026 Hall of Fame class. Kraft has been eligible for the Hall of Fame for years, but last year was the first time he had advanced out of the subcommittee. Former Patriots coach Bill Belichick, in his first year on the ballot, did not get selected for the Hall of Fame, either.

Kraft, 85, has owned the Patriots since 1994. Under his ownership, New England has won six Super Bowls and appeared in five more, including last season's loss to the Seahawks. Prior to Kraft's ownership, the Patriots had only been to one Super Bowl, which it lost. In addition, Kraft has been a key member of several NFL committees, and he helped lead the creation of Gillette Stadium, which opened in 2002.

In 2024, ESPN detailed Kraft's long struggle for a spot in Canton, with various voters pointing to Spygate (when the Patriots taped the Jets' practices), Deflategate and dismissed charges after Kraft's two visits to a Jupiter, Florida, massage parlor as reasons why Kraft hasn't been inducted.

#2543. Lisandro Martinez was stupid, selfish and let the club down: Man United fans may have loved 'The Butcher' but losing his head is the latest act on the road to a bitter Old Trafford exit, writes CHRIS WHEELER

Published: 22:00 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 22:00 EDT, 31 October 2026

To borrow a phrase from Lisandro Martinez, we expect more from him.

We expect more from a vastly experienced defender and World Cup winner. We expect more from a 28-year-old whose team-mates during a stellar career include Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo.

We expect more from Martinez than to fling an arm into the face of an opponent in the penalty box a matter of seconds after being booked for another offence with such a crucial game hanging in the balance.

How did he think he was going to get away with it? How did he think it was going to help Manchester United’s chances of staying out of the relegation zone or Michael Carrick’s prospects of keeping his job?

Just when Carrick needed cool heads among his senior players, Martinez went and lost his.

No sooner had his arm connected with Wesley Fofana than VAR official James Bell sent referee Peter Bankes to the monitor. A second yellow card followed and a penalty for Cole Palmer to convert Chelsea's second goal. Game over.

When Michael Carrick needed cool heads, Lisandro Martinez (right) went and lost his

He finds himself at the scene of the crime too often and his time at the club appears to be coming to an end

There was no way back for United from there, not in their current fragile state.

Carrick couldn’t say what he really thought of Martinez’s moment of madness, but legendary United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel did it for him.

'I put this solely on Lisandro Martinez's shoulders,' fumed Schmeichel. 'This is an absolute disgrace how he played this game. The penalty, I have no words for how crazy that was. Then he walks off the pitch shaking his head like he's done nothing wrong. So bad.'

This is the same Martinez who landed himself with a club fine earlier this month for saying he expected more of United’s director of football Jason Wilcox in the transfer market last summer.

The same Martinez who scored a hapless own-goal down the road from Chelsea at Fulham in September. The same Martinez who turned his back on the ball against Tottenham a week earlier, and allowed Dominic Solanke to score a late equaliser at Old Trafford.

With his contract running out in June, and no sign of United intending to trigger a 12-month extension clause, it looks as though his time at United is coming to an end and not in the way he would have wanted.

‘Whatever the next Man United phase is, I think Martinez's time at the club has run its course,’ Joe Cole told TNT Sports. ‘In a Man United shirt, he's just at the scene of the crime too often.’

No doubt Martinez’s resentment over his contract situation played a part in his comment about Wilcox. While supporters have applauded him for calling out the club’s recruitment – and there is no doubt he has a point – his time would be better spent focussing on keeping the ball out of United’s net and keeping himself on the pitch rather than pointing the finger at others.

He has been one of United’s better signings of recent years, albeit one hampered by a succession of unfortunate injuries. The combative edge and winning mentality he brought from his time with Argentina and Ajax have been an asset to Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and, to a lesser extent, Carrick.

Michael Carrick (left) could not say what he really thought but was let down by one of his more senior players

The fans love The Butcher and you can see why at a time when so many players who have passed through the doors during his five years at Old Trafford have failed to show enough heart for the fight

But this was a stupid, selfish act borne out of frustration which cost United any chance of winning this game and will keep Martinez out of United’s last fixture before the international break at home to Aston Villa next weekend.

By the time they return to action, there is no guarantee Carrick will still be in a job.

If you want to compare Michael Carrick’s successful spell in charge at United last season with the seemingly inexplicable drop-off this term, this was exactly the kind of marginal game that he was winning back then.

Think of Carrick’s first two matches in charge against Manchester City and Arsenal, and the 3-2 wins over Liverpool, Nottingham Forest and Fulham. Perhaps most relevant of all, the 1-0 win here over Chelsea in April when Matheus Cunha scored the only goal just before half-time.

If United had taken only half their chances in the first half at Stamford Bridge this time, they could have put the game to bed. Amad Diallo had enough of them to win it on his own.

It would be easy to say that Carrick’s luck has run out but it isn’t that easy in elite sport. The confidence that flowed through the team in those months between January and May has drained from his players. Chances are being missed, silly goals conceded. Experienced campaigners like Martinez are suffering from a rush of blood to the head, and every mistake is being punished. That’s what happens when the tide turns and you haven’t got the resilience to ride it out.

Every game looks hard for United at the moment. Their only victories this season have been at home to Sabah and Ipswich, and even the latter came with a slice of luck.

Who knows where their next win is coming from? As he left West London looking rather dazed, Carrick didn’t seem like a man who has the answer to that question.

It feels like Bruno Fernandes's great Manchester United career may be coming to an end

Once we knew Carrick would be in the dugout at Stamford Bridge, all the talk in the build-up to this game was about the return of captain Bruno Fernandes after he was dropped for last weekend’s defeat to Bournemouth.

Fernandes didn’t just come back into the line-up, he was back at No10 after vacating that role for Youri Tielemans in recent weeks. Tielemans was deservedly left on the bench here while Fernandes interchanged with Cunha in a fluid United attack that performed well in a promising first half.

But the Fernandes of old would have made his mark on this game. Got a goal or an assist to lead his team to victory and ram the taunts of rival fans down their throats.

But he did nothing of the sort. Too many passes went astray, too often the arms were thrown up in the air in frustration. When he had a great chance to put United ahead in the first half from Bryan Mbeumo’s brilliant pass, Fernandes blazed it over the bar.

One man can’t carry an entire team, but the Portugal star has come close to it at times during his seven-year career at Old Trafford. Here, though, was more evidence that his powers may be fading and this United team may be beyond help.

United were open to selling Fernandes to Al-Hilal last year and won’t break the bank to keep him when his current deal runs out in June. They might renew at the right price or at least trigger the 12-month option to make sure he doesn’t leave on a free transfer.

But it feels like a great United career may be coming to an end.

#2541. Jets' Garrett Wilson enters concussion protocol a week before 2026 NFL trade deadline

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

One of the the top playmakers who could be available at the 2026 NFL trade deadline is now in the concussion protocol.

New York Jets coach Aaron Glenn told reporters on Wednesday that 2022 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year wide receiver Garrett Wilson is in the concussion protocol. Wilson leads the Jets in targets (63), catches (43), receiving yards (527) and receiving touchdowns (3) this season, and his four-year, $130 million contract extension is set to kick in next season.

It sounds inconceivable that the rebuilding Jets would part with a 26-year-old who has been one of the team's faces, but Wilson showed public signs of frustration in their loss to the previously winless Miami Dolphins in Week 7. CBS cameras caught Wilson appearing to yell at quarterback Geno Smith and passing game coordinator Seth Ryan. After the game, Wilson said it was a constructive conversation.

"We were collaborating," said Wilson, via ESPN. "I don't even think I was talking to Geno. I think we were both heated, but not at each other at all. We were just disappointed with how we were playing up to that point and wanted to be a little more aggressive. That's what that was."

Jets WR Garrett Wilson appeared frustrated on the sidelines during the team's loss vs. the Dolphins.(📺 CBS) pic.twitter.com/tMhvk78oC2

Wilson wants to "make an impact" and it will be interesting to see if that will remain to be with the Jets, who are 2-6, long term with the Nov. 10 trade deadline looming.

"Just trying to figure out how we can fix where we're at right now, wanting to get it in our hands and make a difference and try to win these games that we feel like we're a better team -- and we're not," Wilson said. "Like I've said before, I want it in my hands to try and make an impact. So that's all we were talking about, just putting it in our hands and how we can make that happen, being aggressive throughout and keeping ourselves out of those situations so we can win these games."

#2540. Lions' Jack Campbell issues statement updating condition after scary injury vs. Vikings

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a neck injury during the team's eventual Week 8 victory against the Minnesota Vikings. Following a tackle of tight end T.J. Hockenson, the 26-year-old was strapped to a backboard and carted off the field. He remained on his stomach for several minutes after the collision and was not seen moving while trainers attended to him.

The Lions were initially mum on any updates regarding Campbell. On Monday, the team announced he was resting and recovering at a local hospital, but that preliminary indications were "positive."

On Wednesday, Campbell issued a statement himself through the team and revealed that he has full movement in his lower body. He's continuing to make progress with movement in his upper body. However, he said he remains "very optimistic," even though he knows "there's still work ahead."

"My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we've received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express.

I'm incredibly encouraged by the progress I've made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better.

My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we'll get through this.

I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field. I know those were difficult moments, and I'm incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I'll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you.

I also can't say enough about the incredible care I've received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They've been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I'm truly grateful for everything they've done.

To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I'm proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn't ask to be surrounded by a better group of people.

One thing I've learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That's exactly how I'm going to approach this challenge.

Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can't thank everyone enough.

"Anytime, especially being able to hear it from him, that means a lot. That's powerful in itself, more than hearing it from me or anybody else," Lions head coach Dan Campbell told reporters on Wednesday. "Those are his and his family's words, so that's powerful. I know that always helps to know that he's improving. Because at this point, that's all you're looking for, is just to know that he's improving. The status is changing every eight hours, 10 hours, in a good way. It always is going to help."

Campbell is in his fourth season with the Lions. The Iowa product was selected with the No. 18 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft and signed a four-year, $81 million extension that made him one of the highest-paid off-ball linebackers in the NFL this past offseason.

In 2025, Campbell was named a First Team All-Pro and Pro Bowler after recording 176 tackles, nine tackles for loss, five sacks, three forced fumbles and four passes defended.

#2539. MLB free agency: Predicting landing spots for top players, including Jazz Chisholm Jr., Freddy Peralta, more

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Free agency is officially open. As of Monday, five days after the Milwaukee Brewers clinched the first World Series title in franchise history, eligible players are able to talk to and negotiate with all 30 teams with the hopes of finding their new employer. Some will get long-term deals worth more than most of us could ever dream of.

So who goes where? That's for agents and general managers to figure out. We already covered Tarik Skubal, so your CBS Sports experts are digging a bit deeper down the list for a new round of guessing games.

Mike Axisa: There are already rumblings that Morejon wants to start in 2027 and I reckon more than a few teams will be willing to give him that opportunity. The Cubs need all kinds of pitching, both starters and relievers, and can make it work even if Morejon can't hack it as a starter and needs to return to the bullpen. Regardless of role, he's an excellent pitcher, and few teams need as much pitching as the Cubs this winter. It's a perfect match.

Dayn Perry: Any team can use a lockdown reliever like Morejon, who's also young for a free agent. He's got the repertoire to be a starter conversion, too. The Yankees could use him, of course, and I expect they'll pay what it takes.

Matt Snyder: The Cubs badly need rotation help and Wrigley Field, thanks to Chicago wind patterns, is better suited for left-handed pitchers. The ownership there spends money, yes, but is relatively cheap given their market and money-making ability, which means they'll cheap out on Tarik Skubal (if they even try seriously, and my guess is they won't). So they'll need consolation prizes (yes, plural). Morejon will convert to starting and be one of them.

Mike Axisa: Rogers is underrated and he'll have an awful lot of suitors among teams that rely heavily on analytical models this offseason. He has four pitches that grade out as above average, plus he's already demonstrated the ability to get chase out of the zone and limit weak contact. It feels like he's a tweak or two away from becoming a frontline starter, or very close to one. The Mets match up well. They're data-heavy and they need a starting pitcher.

Dayn Perry: Even with some injured arms in line to return at various points in 2027, the Cubs still need rotation help, especially since they share a division with the champion Brewers. I can't see the Ricketts family, who doesn't spend nearly as much it should given the deep coffers the Cubs have, paying for Tarik Skubal. So Rogers it is, since he's arguably the second-best rotation arm on the market.

Matt Snyder: The Braves were hit with a litany of pitching injuries last season and still won the division, but there are a ton of question marks here. Spencer Strider and Spencer Schwellenbach are on that list for sure, but what about Chris Sale? He's heading toward his age-37 year and there's a club option for 2028 before he hits free agency. Grabbing Rogers here provides immediate help, depth and -- assuming it's a long-term deal -- an option to take over as the top lefty once Sale is out.

Mike Axisa: The Cubs have long been rumored as a landing spot for Peralta because of the Craig Counsell connection, though I like the other Chicago team as a fit better. The White Sox are on the rise and they badly need starting pitching. Openers and bullpen games work great in moderation. When you're doing it three or four times each turn through the rotation, it's too much. Peralta will take the ball every five days like clockwork and he's a pretty darn good pitcher too. The ChiSox need both the reliability and upside.

Dayn Perry: Yeah, I'm going with the upset here. Peralta improved significantly under the Rays' watch after the deadline deal that brought him there from the Mets, which means this tracks as a mutually beneficial relationship. With a new ballpark all but assured and a forthcoming CBA that should benefit smaller markets -- and with Stu Sternberg no longer in charge -- the Rays may be poised to actually spend a little.

Matt Snyder: We know that Jerry Dipoto doesn't like to sit still and after the Mariners came within one win of their first World Series, they were bad in 2026. They are still built to win now, especially in an awful division, but they'll reshape the team. I could see trades of starters Logan Gilbert and/or George Kirby that create the need for a rotation replacement in free agency, and Peralta would surely love pitching in that ballpark.

Mike Axisa: Ernie Clement crashed hard in the second half and has always fit better as a super utility guy who moves around rather than someone who plays one set position every day. The Blue Jays desperately need a power infusion, particularly from the left side of the plate, and Chisholm's defense and baserunning will fit in nicely as well. I wonder if any teams would show interest in Chisholm at third base or center field, two positions he's played in the past. Second base in Toronto is my best guess for now.

Dayn Perry: Detroit had pretty good luck with another outgoing Yankees second baseman (Gleyber Torres), so why not another? Jazz is coming off a down season, but he's not far removed from a 2025 campaign that was one of his best ever. A mid-term deal with opt outs aplenty makes sense here, or maybe even a high-AAV one-year pact.

Matt Snyder: There are two picks in one here, as I'll predict the Diamondbacks trade Ketel Marte and that leaves an opening to grab Chisholm for second base. It might be a one-year deal where Chisholm bets on himself to bounce back from a huge step back from his career year in 2025.

Mike Axisa: President of baseball operations Chris Young has already talked about his team needing more grit and being better at rising to the occasion offensively. That's Arozarena, who can be a flashy player but is also tough and hard-nosed, and has shown time and time again that he is unafraid of big moments. He needs to DH full-time at this point in his career and the Rangers can give him that runway. A righty power bat to complement Brandon Nimmo and Corey Seager feels imperative.

Dayn Perry: Arozarena is coming off an excellent season with Seattle, and the Phillies, still trying to make the most of their closing window, badly need an upgrade at the outfield corners. Philly hasn't been shy about investing in the on-field product, which means adding the likes of Arozarena would be fully in character.

Matt Snyder: The Phillies' window of contention remains open, even if not for long, and team president Dave Dombrowski isn't shy about adding short-term fixes to his roster. Adolis Garcia didn't work out last year, but that doesn't mean Dombrowski will be shy this time around. They still want to win a World Series with this nucleus and they need corner outfield help, among other things.

#2538. Eagles to start Joe Milton at quarterback vs. Giants, replacing Tanner McKee

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Philadelphia Eagles are entrusting a former Dallas Cowboy to be their new starting quarterback. Joe Milton will be the team's starting quarterback in Week 9 against the NFC East-leading New York Giants, per ESPN.

Milton will be the third Eagles starting quarterback this season after Jalen Hurts went on injured reserve and backup Tanner McKee lost all three of his starts. The Eagles scooped him up off of the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad on Oct. 16, a day before Hurts went on IR.

"I think he's worked really hard," Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said Wednesday morning, via NBC Sports Philadelphia. "Him and [quarterbacks coach] Parks [Frazier] have spent a ton of time together, getting him caught up to speed. I know the developmental periods; those always help to be able to run our plays. But he works extremely hard. He is always in the building, doing the extra things. I like his progression."

Milton could bring the deep ball back to the Eagles' offense. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer has compared Milton's arm strength to that of Brett Favre. However, Schottenheimer also expressed reservations about Milton's game, particularly his accuracy and touch. That's why Sam Howell won the Dallas backup job, leaving Milton as Dallas' No. 3 quarterback on the practice squad and up for grabs for Philadelphia to scoop him up. The Cowboys originally acquired Milton, a 2024 sixth-round pick, in April of 2025 in a trade with the New England Patriots, and he served as Dak Prescott's backup in 2025.

This preseason, Milton showed significant strides in both areas when the lights came on in Dallas' three exhibition games: he completed 29 of his 43 passes (67.4%) for 378 yards, three passing touchdowns and no interceptions for a 118.2 passer rating.

"I'm going to say that the upside, I'm not going to say you put him into a box of what he could be, but the arm talent's real," Schottenheimer said in camp. "I think we've talked a lot in here about the touch and how he's developed the touch. I do know that he did a much better job with our system. This is what guys that come from that spread system [in college] have to deal with in terms of the learning curve of coming in and having to learn how to huddle, call a play in the huddle and make different decisions. ... I think about that. ... So again, I think Joe's going to be a terrific player in this league. I'm not going to say in what regard, but like I said, it was a very tough decision."

#2537. Führich reflects on missed turning point in Galatasaray defeat

Stuttgart suffered their first defeat of their Champions League campaign in Istanbul, with Aleksey Batrakov scoring twice in the opening 15 minutes to secure a 2-0 win for Galatasaray.

VfB had made an encouraging start, with Jamie Leweling striking both posts with the same effort after just eight minutes.

The visitors then improved considerably after the interval, and thought they had found a route back into the contest when Chris Führich found the net from range, only for his effort to be ruled out for an offside against Deniz Undav.

Speaking to DAZN after the final whistle, the 28-year-old reflected on a frustrating evening in Istanbul.

“We invested a great deal. We started exactly as we had planned, with a huge chance for Jamie. If that goes in, it's obviously a completely different situation,” Führich explained.

"Then we conceded the first goal because we were a little too passive, and suddenly there's an energy here that you have to withstand.

"The second goal came straight afterwards, which was very bitter.

“We recovered quite well. I think we played a good game in the second half, with lots of chances and a few situations we could have played out better. But in the end, we were missing the goal.”

The German international was Stuttgart's best player on the night, and was particularly disappointed that his second-half strike was disallowed, believing that it could have provided Die Schwaben with a way back into the contest.

"It's a shame about the offside goal. I think that could have been another turning point, but it wasn't to be.

“We gave everything, put everything into the game, and I think we can still take a lot of positives away from here.”
